title: Repeated maxima and negative terminal corners

blocks.tex:
This chapter proves the remaining two physical producers used in
\cref{thm:four_active_adjacent_unequal}: the \emph{equal-pure} producer at
two occurrences of the global maximum, and the \emph{negative-corner}
producer at a highest secondary peak whose two terminal first-pair flags
are negative.  Both are proved in Lean; the chapter explains the proofs.  The
final statements are \cref{thm:nrn_repeated_anchor} and
\cref{thm:nrn_negative_anchor}.

Both producers live on the native four-edge model of
\cref{def:nfp_native_model}: starts $(1,t,q,l)$, finishes $(p,q,h,1)$,
positive \emph{half}-lengths $L_0,\dots,L_3$ and the eight literal endpoint
walls
\[
  L_0<1,\quad pL_0<1,\quad tL_1<1,\quad qL_1<1,\quad qL_2<1,\quad
  hL_2<1,\quad lL_3<1,\quad L_3<1 .
\]
In contrast with \cref{chap:discrete_native_first_pair}, here \emph{every}
mixed endpoint reading lies strictly below its incident pure reading:
\[
  0<p,l<1,\qquad 0<t,h<q,\qquad q\ge1 .
\]
The equal-pure producer has $q=1$ (both pure readings are maxima); the
negative-corner producer has $q>1$.  The argument has four parts.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Roots} (\cref{sec:nrn_repeated} and \cref{sec:nrn_negative}).
    A zero of the two original mixed-turn residuals on the orthogonal core
    of curvatures $(1,u,q,v)$ is a native zero; all eight walls hold.  For
    $q=1$ an interior rectangle with uniform face signs and the
    Poincar\'e--Miranda theorem give the zero; for $q>1$ a clamped square
    with signs only at boundary zeros does.
  \item \textbf{Incident rank, nonacute chamber} (\cref{sec:nrn_incident}).
    If the second pure turn $T=\gamma+\delta$ is at least a right angle, an
    explicit $3\times3$ derivative in coordinates $(S,\alpha,T)$ is
    invertible.  For $q=1$ this is always the case.
  \item \textbf{Incident rank, acute chamber} (\cref{sec:nrn_acute}).  At a
    core zero with $T<\pi/2$, rank loss forces two actual derivative minors
    to vanish; exact core trigonometry turns this into a polynomial system
    (\verb|IncidentProjectiveRankLoss|), and an exact elimination with a sign
    argument shows that it has no solution.
  \item \textbf{Selection} (\cref{sec:nrn_selection}).  The four literal
    edges incident to the two peaks form a frame with exactly these endpoint
    readings, and the native zero becomes a regular four-edge anchor
    (\cref{def:regular_four_anchor}) of the original word.
\end{enumerate}
No step assumes a producer, a nondegeneracy hypothesis, a numerical sign or
a determinant certificate.

blocks.label: lem:nrn_poincare_miranda_rect
blocks.title: Poincar\'e--Miranda on a rectangle
blocks.body:
Let $a_1\le a_2$, $b_1\le b_2$ and $G\colon\RR^2\to\RR^2$ continuous on
  $K=[a_1,a_2]\times[b_1,b_2]$ with $G_1(a_1,y)\le0\le G_1(a_2,y)$ for
  $y\in[b_1,b_2]$ and $G_2(x,b_1)\le0\le G_2(x,b_2)$ for $x\in[a_1,a_2]$.
  Then $G$ has a zero in $K$.

blocks.tex:
This is \cref{thm:discrete_poincare_miranda_rect} restated under a project
  name; the Lean declaration is a one-line wrapper around
  \verb|poincare_miranda|.  It lives in a file of the hyperbolic library but
  uses no hyperbolic geometry.

We use the literal mixed residuals $R_1(u,v)=\operatorname{R}_1(p,t,q;u,v)$
and $R_3(u,v)=\operatorname{R}_3(q,h,l;u,v)$ of
\cref{def:nfp_ordered_residual}, with the parameter $q$ now allowed to be
$1$.  Explicitly, with $d=\sqrt{q^2-u^2v^2}$,
\begin{align*}
  R_1&=\arcsin\Bigl(p\tfrac{\sqrt{q^2-v^2}}d\Bigr)
      +\arcsin\Bigl(t\tfrac{\sqrt{1-v^2}}d\Bigr)
      -\arcsin\Bigl(u\tfrac{\sqrt{q^2-v^2}}d\Bigr)
      -\arcsin\Bigl(u\tfrac{\sqrt{1-v^2}}d\Bigr),\\
  R_3&=\arcsin\Bigl(h\tfrac{\sqrt{1-u^2}}d\Bigr)
      +\arcsin\Bigl(l\tfrac{\sqrt{q^2-u^2}}d\Bigr)
      -\arcsin\Bigl(v\tfrac{\sqrt{1-u^2}}d\Bigr)
      -\arcsin\Bigl(v\tfrac{\sqrt{q^2-u^2}}d\Bigr),
\end{align*}
with the principal arcsine, and $\mathcal R=R_1+iR_3$
(\verb|rResidualMap p t q h l|).  These are formulas on all of $\RR^2$; the
rectangle $[p,1]\times[l,1]$ of \cref{def:nfp_ordered_residual} is only the
domain used in the ordered branch.

blocks.label: lem:nrn_residual_basics
blocks.title: reflection and continuity of the residuals
blocks.body:
For all real $q,h,l,u,v$,
  \[
    \operatorname{R}_3(q,h,l;u,v)=\operatorname{R}_1(l,h,q;v,u).
  \]
  Both residuals are continuous on every set on which $q^2-u^2v^2>0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.N6TypeAThreeCell.continuousOn_rResidualThree_of_denom_pos
lean.code:
theorem continuousOn_rResidualThree_of_denom_pos
    {q h l : ℝ} {s : Set (ℝ × ℝ)}
    (hden : ∀ z ∈ s, 0 < q ^ 2 - z.1 ^ 2 * z.2 ^ 2) :
    ContinuousOn (fun z ↦ rResidualThree q h l z.1 z.2) s := by
  let d : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ := fun z ↦ √(q ^ 2 - z.1 ^ 2 * z.2 ^ 2)
  let c : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ := fun z ↦ √(1 - z.1 ^ 2) / d z
  let e : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ := fun z ↦ √(q ^ 2 - z.1 ^ 2) / d z
  have hd : Continuous d := by
    dsimp only [d]
    fun_prop
  have hdNe : ∀ z ∈ s, d z ≠ 0 :=
    fun z hz ↦ (Real.sqrt_pos.2 (hden z hz)).ne'
  have hc : ContinuousOn c s := by
    dsimp only [c]
    exact (by fun_prop : Continuous fun z : ℝ × ℝ ↦ √(1 - z.1 ^ 2)).continuousOn.div
      hd.continuousOn hdNe
  have he : ContinuousOn e s := by
    dsimp only [e]
    exact (by fun_prop : Continuous fun z : ℝ × ℝ ↦ √(q ^ 2 - z.1 ^ 2)).continuousOn.div
      hd.continuousOn hdNe
  change ContinuousOn (fun z ↦ Real.arcsin (h * c z) + Real.arcsin (l * e z) -
    Real.arcsin (z.2 * c z) - Real.arcsin (z.2 * e z)) s
  exact (((continuousOn_const.mul hc).arcsin.add
    (continuousOn_const.mul he).arcsin).sub
      (continuousOn_snd.mul hc).arcsin).sub (continuousOn_snd.mul he).arcsin

lemma rResidualThree_eq_swap (q h l u v : ℝ) :
    rResidualThree q h l u v = rResidualOne l h q v u := by
  unfold rResidualThree rResidualOne
  rw [mul_comm (v ^ 2) (u ^ 2)]
  ring

theorem continuousOn_rResidualOne_of_denom_pos
    {p t q : ℝ} {s : Set (ℝ × ℝ)}
    (hden : ∀ z ∈ s, 0 < q ^ 2 - z.1 ^ 2 * z.2 ^ 2) :
    ContinuousOn (fun z ↦ rResidualOne p t q z.1 z.2) s := by
  let d : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ := fun z ↦ √(q ^ 2 - z.1 ^ 2 * z.2 ^ 2)
  let a : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ := fun z ↦ √(q ^ 2 - z.2 ^ 2) / d z
  let b : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ := fun z ↦ √(1 - z.2 ^ 2) / d z
  have hd : Continuous d := by
    dsimp only [d]
    fun_prop
  have hdNe : ∀ z ∈ s, d z ≠ 0 :=
    fun z hz ↦ (Real.sqrt_pos.2 (hden z hz)).ne'
  have ha : ContinuousOn a s := by
    dsimp only [a]
    exact (by fun_prop : Continuous fun z : ℝ × ℝ ↦ √(q ^ 2 - z.2 ^ 2)).continuousOn.div
      hd.continuousOn hdNe
  have hb : ContinuousOn b s := by
    dsimp only [b]
    exact (by fun_prop : Continuous fun z : ℝ × ℝ ↦ √(1 - z.2 ^ 2)).continuousOn.div
      hd.continuousOn hdNe
  change ContinuousOn (fun z ↦ Real.arcsin (p * a z) + Real.arcsin (t * b z) -
    Real.arcsin (z.1 * a z) - Real.arcsin (z.1 * b z)) s
  exact (((continuousOn_const.mul ha).arcsin.add
    (continuousOn_const.mul hb).arcsin).sub
      (continuousOn_fst.mul ha).arcsin).sub (continuousOn_fst.mul hb).arcsin

blocks.tex:
In $\operatorname{R}_1(l,h,q;v,u)$ the roles of $u$ and $v$ are exchanged,
  so its two scale factors are $\sqrt{q^2-u^2}/d$ and $\sqrt{1-u^2}/d$, with
  the same $d$ because $v^2u^2=u^2v^2$.  Matching the four arcsine terms one
  by one ($l\leftrightarrow$ the $\sqrt{q^2-u^2}$ scale, $h\leftrightarrow$
  the $\sqrt{1-u^2}$ scale) gives exactly $\operatorname{R}_3(q,h,l;u,v)$.
  Continuity: $d$ is continuous and nonzero where $q^2-u^2v^2>0$, the two
  quotients are continuous there, and $\arcsin$ is continuous on $\RR$.

The reflection identity is the algebraic form of reversing the orientation
of the four-edge model: it exchanges the mixed slots $(p,t)$ and $(h,l)$
and the core variables $u$ and $v$.  It turns every statement about $R_1$ on
a face $u=\text{const}$ into a statement about $R_3$ on the face
$v=\text{const}$.

blocks.label: lem:nrn_equal_core
blocks.title: the equal-pure orthogonal core
blocks.body:
Let $0<u,v<1$.  The orthogonal quadrilateral with curvatures $(1,u,1,v)$
  has $\Delta=1-u^2v^2>0$ and half-sides
  \[
    \frac A2=\frac B2=\frac{\sqrt{1-v^2}}{\sqrt{1-u^2v^2}},\qquad
    \frac C2=\frac D2=\frac{\sqrt{1-u^2}}{\sqrt{1-u^2v^2}},
  \]
  all positive, and $(A,B,C,D)$ is a strict moderate-arc development of
  $(1,u,1,v)$ with exact closure and real total turn $2\pi$ (it is also
  simple).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.N6TypeAThreeCell.r_core_sides_pos
lean.code:
lemma r_core_sides_pos {k u q v : ℝ}
    (hk : 0 < k) (hu : 0 < u) (hq : 0 < q) (hv : 0 < v)
    (huk : u < k) (huq : u < q) (hvk : v < k) (hvq : v < q) :
    0 < rCoreSideA k u q v ∧ 0 < rCoreSideB k u q v ∧
      0 < rCoreSideC k u q v ∧ 0 < rCoreSideD k u q v := by
  have hDelta := orthogonal_delta_pos_of_strict_alternation
    hk hu hq hv huk huq hvk hvq
  have hqv := square_sub_pos hv hvq
  have hkv := square_sub_pos hv hvk
  have hku := square_sub_pos hu huk
  have hqu := square_sub_pos hu huq
  simp only [rCoreSideA, rCoreSideB, rCoreSideC, rCoreSideD]
  exact ⟨div_pos (mul_pos two_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hqv)) (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hDelta),
    div_pos (mul_pos two_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hkv)) (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hDelta),
    div_pos (mul_pos two_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hku)) (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hDelta),
    div_pos (mul_pos two_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hqu)) (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hDelta)⟩

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.N6TypeAThreeCell.r_core_realization_data
lean.code:
theorem r_core_realization_data {k u q v : ℝ}
    (hk : 0 < k) (hu : 0 < u) (hq : 0 < q) (hv : 0 < v)
    (huk : u < k) (huq : u < q) (hvk : v < k) (hvq : v < q) :
    ModerateArc 0 (fourProfile k u q v)
        (fourProfile (rCoreSideA k u q v) (rCoreSideB k u q v)
          (rCoreSideC k u q v) (rCoreSideD k u q v)) ∧
      closureGap (fourProfile k u q v)
          (fourProfile (rCoreSideA k u q v) (rCoreSideB k u q v)
            (rCoreSideC k u q v) (rCoreSideD k u q v)) = 0 ∧
      turningSum (fourProfile k u q v)
          (fourProfile (rCoreSideA k u q v) (rCoreSideB k u q v)
            (rCoreSideC k u q v) (rCoreSideD k u q v)) = 2 * Real.pi ∧
      IsSimplePolygon (polygonR2 (fourProfile k u q v)
        (fourProfile (rCoreSideA k u q v) (rCoreSideB k u q v)
          (rCoreSideC k u q v) (rCoreSideD k u q v))) := by
  let A := rCoreSideA k u q v
  let B := rCoreSideB k u q v
  let C := rCoreSideC k u q v
  let D := rCoreSideD k u q v
  let a := rCoreHalfDiagonalA k u q v
  let b := rCoreHalfDiagonalB k u q v
  let c := rCoreHalfDiagonalC k u q v
  let d := rCoreHalfDiagonalD k u q v
  have hDelta := orthogonal_delta_pos_of_strict_alternation
    hk hu hq hv huk huq hvk hvq
  have hqv := square_sub_pos hv hvq
  have hkv := square_sub_pos hv hvk
  have hku := square_sub_pos hu huk
  have hqu := square_sub_pos hu huq
  obtain ⟨hA, hB, hC, hD⟩ : 0 < A ∧ 0 < B ∧ 0 < C ∧ 0 < D := by
    simpa only [A, B, C, D] using
      r_core_sides_pos hk hu hq hv huk huq hvk hvq
  obtain ⟨ha, hb, hc, hd⟩ : 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 < d := by
    simpa only [a, b, c, d] using
      r_core_half_diagonals_pos hk hu hq hv huk huq hvk hvq
  have hAroot : A ^ 2 = orthogonalA2 k u q v := by
    simpa only [A] using r_core_side_a_sq hDelta.le hqv.le
  have hBroot : B ^ 2 = orthogonalB2 k u q v := by
    simpa only [B] using r_core_side_b_sq hDelta.le hkv.le
  have hCroot : C ^ 2 = orthogonalC2 k u q v := by
    simpa only [C] using r_core_side_c_sq hDelta.le hku.le
  have hDroot : D ^ 2 = orthogonalD2 k u q v := by
    simpa only [D] using r_core_side_d_sq hDelta.le hqu.le
  have hasq : a ^ 2 = k ^ 2 * A ^ 2 * D ^ 2 / 4 := by
    change (k * A * D / 2) ^ 2 = k ^ 2 * A ^ 2 * D ^ 2 / 4
    ring
  have hbsq : b ^ 2 = u ^ 2 * A ^ 2 * B ^ 2 / 4 := by
    change (u * A * B / 2) ^ 2 = u ^ 2 * A ^ 2 * B ^ 2 / 4
    ring
  have hcsq : c ^ 2 = q ^ 2 * B ^ 2 * C ^ 2 / 4 := by
    change (q * B * C / 2) ^ 2 = q ^ 2 * B ^ 2 * C ^ 2 / 4
    ring
  have hdsq : d ^ 2 = v ^ 2 * C ^ 2 * D ^ 2 / 4 := by
    change (v * C * D / 2) ^ 2 = v ^ 2 * C ^ 2 * D ^ 2 / 4
    ring
  have hAsq : A ^ 2 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 := by
    rw [hAroot, hasq, hbsq, hAroot, hBroot, hDroot]
    exact orthogonalA2_identity hDelta.ne'
  have hBsq : B ^ 2 = b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 := by
    rw [hBroot, hbsq, hcsq, hAroot, hBroot, hCroot]
  -- … (truncated)

deps.title: the orthogonal quadrilateral is a moderate development
deps.label: thm:n4c_realization_data

blocks.tex:
The Lean statements \verb|r_core_realization_data| and
  \verb|r_core_sides_pos| are proved for a general core $(k,u,q,v)$ under
  the strict alternation $0<k,u,q,v$, $u<k$, $u<q$, $v<k$, $v<q$.  We apply
  them with $k=q=1$: the alternation reads $u<1$ and $v<1$, which is our
  hypothesis.  This is a direct instance, not a limit $q\downarrow1$ of
  \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_core} (whose statement assumes $q>1$).

  Concretely, $\Delta(1,u,1,v)=1\cdot1-u^2v^2=(1-uv)(1+uv)>0$ since
  $0<uv<1$.  The side formulas of \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_core},
  $A/2=\sqrt{q^2-v^2}/d$, $B/2=\sqrt{k^2-v^2}/d$, $C/2=\sqrt{k^2-u^2}/d$,
  $D/2=\sqrt{q^2-u^2}/d$ with $d=\sqrt\Delta$, are the Lean definitions
  \verb|rCoreSideA|--\verb|rCoreSideD| divided by two, and at $k=q=1$ they
  become the displayed values; all radicands are positive.  The four
  side-square identities of \cref{lem:n4c_identityA}, \cref{lem:n4c_identityB},
  \cref{lem:n4c_identityC} and \cref{lem:n4c_identityD} hold whenever $\Delta\ne0$, and \cref{thm:n4c_realization_data} gives the
  moderate-arc closure with total turn $2\pi$ exactly as in the proof of
  \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_core}.

At $q=1$ both scales of $R_1$ coincide:
$a(u,v)=\sqrt{1-v^2}/\sqrt{1-u^2v^2}$, and
\[
  R_1(u,v)=\arcsin(pa)+\arcsin(ta)-2\arcsin(ua).
\]

lemma equalPeak_first_residual_neg {p t u v : ℝ}

blocks.label: thm:nrn_repeated_root
blocks.title: a residual zero between two repeated maxima
blocks.body:
Let $p,t,h,l\in(0,1)$.  Then there is $(u,v)\in(0,1)^2$ with
  $\mathcal R(u,v)=0$ for the residuals with $q=1$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.exists_r_zero_of_repeated_maximum
lean.code:
theorem exists_r_zero_of_repeated_maximum {p t h l : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (ht : 0 < t) (ht1 : t < 1)
    (hh : 0 < h) (hh1 : h < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1) :
    ∃ z ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, rResidualMap p t 1 h l z = 0 := by
  let a := min (min p t) (min h l) / 2
  let b := (1 + max (max p t) (max h l)) / 2
  have ha0 : 0 < a := half_pos (lt_min (lt_min hp ht) (lt_min hh hl))
  have hap : a < p := by dsimp [a]; linarith [min_le_left p t, min_le_left (min p t) (min h l)]
  have hat : a < t := by dsimp [a]; linarith [min_le_right p t, min_le_left (min p t) (min h l)]
  have hah : a < h := by dsimp [a]; linarith [min_le_left h l, min_le_right (min p t) (min h l)]
  have hal : a < l := by dsimp [a]; linarith [min_le_right h l, min_le_right (min p t) (min h l)]
  have hb1 : b < 1 := by
    have := max_lt (max_lt hp1 ht1) (max_lt hh1 hl1)
    dsimp [b]; linarith
  have hpb : p < b := by dsimp [b]; linarith [le_max_left p t, le_max_left (max p t) (max h l)]
  have htb : t < b := by dsimp [b]; linarith [le_max_right p t, le_max_left (max p t) (max h l)]
  have hhb : h < b := by dsimp [b]; linarith [le_max_left h l, le_max_right (max p t) (max h l)]
  have hlb : l < b := by dsimp [b]; linarith [le_max_right h l, le_max_right (max p t) (max h l)]
  have hab : a < b := hap.trans hpb
  have hsub : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, x ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 :=
    fun x hx => ⟨ha0.trans_le hx.1, hx.2.trans_lt hb1⟩
  have ha : a ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 := hsub a ⟨le_rfl, hab.le⟩
  have hb : b ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 := hsub b ⟨hab.le, le_rfl⟩
  have hden : ∀ z ∈ Icc a b ×ˢ Icc a b, 0 < (1 : ℝ)^2 - z.1^2 * z.2^2 := by
    intro z hz
    simpa using equalPeak_denom_pos (hsub z.1 hz.1) (hsub z.2 hz.2)
  let R : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ × ℝ := fun z =>
    (-rResidualOne p t 1 z.1 z.2, -rResidualThree 1 h l z.1 z.2)
  have hR : ContinuousOn R (Icc a b ×ˢ Icc a b) :=
    (continuousOn_rResidualOne_of_denom_pos (p := p) (t := t) hden).neg.prodMk
      (continuousOn_rResidualThree_of_denom_pos (h := h) (l := l) hden).neg
  obtain ⟨z, hz, hzero⟩ := poincare_miranda hab.le hab.le R hR
    (fun v hv => neg_nonpos.mpr (equalPeak_first_residual_pos hp1 ht1 ha (hsub v hv) hap hat).le)
    (fun v hv => neg_nonneg.mpr (equalPeak_first_residual_neg hp ht hb (hsub v hv) hpb htb).le)
    (fun u hu => by
      change -rResidualThree 1 h l u a ≤ 0
      rw [rResidualThree_eq_swap]
      exact neg_nonpos.mpr (equalPeak_first_residual_pos hl1 hh1 ha (hsub u hu) hal hah).le)
    (fun u hu => by
      change 0 ≤ -rResidualThree 1 h l u b
      rw [rResidualThree_eq_swap]
      exact neg_nonneg.mpr (equalPeak_first_residual_neg hl hh hb (hsub u hu) hlb hhb).le)
  refine ⟨z, ⟨hsub z.1 hz.1, hsub z.2 hz.2⟩, ?_⟩
  apply Complex.ext
  · have hF := congrArg Prod.fst hzero
    change -rResidualOne p t 1 z.1 z.2 = 0 at hF
    simpa only [r_residual_map_re, Complex.zero_re] using neg_eq_zero.mp hF
  · have hG := congrArg Prod.snd hzero
    change -rResidualThree 1 h l z.1 z.2 = 0 at hG
    simpa only [r_residual_map_im, Complex.zero_im] using neg_eq_zero.mp hG

deps.title: reflection and continuity of the residuals
deps.label: lem:nrn_residual_basics

blocks.tex:
Put
  \[
    a=\tfrac12\min(p,t,h,l),\qquad b=\tfrac12\bigl(1+\max(p,t,h,l)\bigr).
  \]
  Then $0<a<p,t,h,l<b<1$; in particular $0<a<b<1$.  On $[a,b]^2$ every
  coordinate lies in $(0,1)$, so $1-u^2v^2>0$ and both residuals are
  continuous there (\cref{lem:nrn_residual_basics}).  Apply
  \cref{lem:nrn_poincare_miranda_rect} on $[a,b]^2$ to $G=(-R_1,-R_3)$:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item left face $u=a$: $a<p,t$, so $R_1>0$ by
      \cref{lem:nrn_equal_signs}(1) and $G_1\le0$;
    \item right face $u=b$: $p,t<b$, so $R_1<0$ by
      \cref{lem:nrn_equal_signs}(2) and $G_1\ge0$;
    \item bottom face $v=a$: by reflection $R_3(u,a)=\operatorname{R}_1(l,h,1;a,u)$,
      positive by \cref{lem:nrn_equal_signs}(1) since $a<l,h$; so $G_2\le0$;
    \item top face $v=b$: $R_3(u,b)=\operatorname{R}_1(l,h,1;b,u)<0$ since
      $l,h<b$; so $G_2\ge0$.
  \end{itemize}
  The face signs are in fact strict and uniform.  The zero $(u,v)\in[a,b]^2$
  of $G$ is a zero of $R_1$ and $R_3$, hence of $\mathcal R$, and lies in
  $(0,1)^2$.

  The inner rectangle is essential: at $q=1$ the denominator
  $1-u^2v^2$ vanishes at the outer corner $(1,1)$ of the unit square, where
  the residuals are not continuous.  No uniqueness of the zero is used.

blocks.title: an equal-pure residual zero is a native zero
blocks.body:
Let $u,v\in(0,1)$ with $\mathcal R(u,v)=0$ (at $q=1$) and let
  $L=L^{\mathrm{core}}(u,v)=(A/2,B/2,C/2,D/2)$ be the half-sides of
  \cref{lem:nrn_equal_core} (\verb|orderedCoreHalfLengths u 1 v|).  Then
  $N(L)=0$ for the native model with readings $(p,t,1,h,l)$: exact
  closure and $\theta_0+\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3=2\pi$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.native_zero_of_repeated_r_zero
lean.code:
theorem native_zero_of_repeated_r_zero {p t h l u v : ℝ}
    (hu : u ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hv : v ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (hz : rResidualMap p t 1 h l (u, v) = 0) :
    nativeLengthController p t 1 h l (orderedCoreHalfLengths u 1 v) = 0 := by
  have hd := r_core_realization_data zero_lt_one hu.1 zero_lt_one hv.1
    hu.2 hu.2 hv.2 hv.2
  have hcore := equalPeak_native_zero_of_four_realization hd.2.1 hd.2.2.1
  have hr1 : rResidualOne p t 1 u v = 0 := by
    simpa [rResidualMap] using congrArg Complex.re hz
  have hr3 : rResidualThree 1 h l u v = 0 := by
    simpa [rResidualMap] using congrArg Complex.im hz
  rw [r_residual_one_eq_core_sides] at hr1
  rw [r_residual_three_eq_core_sides] at hr3
  have hturn : lengthTurns p t 1 h l (orderedCoreHalfLengths u 1 v) =
      lengthTurns u u 1 v v (orderedCoreHalfLengths u 1 v) := by
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> dsimp [lengthTurns, orderedCoreHalfLengths] <;> linarith
  unfold nativeLengthController
  rw [hturn]
  exact hcore

blocks.tex:
\emph{Turns.}  The native turns of \cref{def:nfp_native_model} for the
  readings $(p,t,1,h,l)$ and for the core readings $(u,u,1,v,v)$ agree slot
  by slot at $L$: $\theta_0=\arcsin L_3+\arcsin L_0$ and
  $\theta_2=\arcsin L_1+\arcsin L_2$ do not involve mixed readings, the
  difference of the $\theta_1$'s is
  $\arcsin(pA/2)+\arcsin(tB/2)-\arcsin(uA/2)-\arcsin(uB/2)=R_1(u,v)=0$, and
  the difference of the $\theta_3$'s is $R_3(u,v)=0$ (identities
  \verb|r_residual_one_eq_core_sides|, \verb|r_residual_three_eq_core_sides|).
  Hence $N_{(p,t,1,h,l)}(L)=N_{(u,u,1,v,v)}(L)$.

  \emph{Core closure.}  In the development of $(1,u,1,v)$ with lengths
  $(A,B,C,D)$ of \cref{lem:nrn_equal_core}, the turning angle at vertex $j$
  is the sum of the two endpoint arcsines of the incident edges; these are
  exactly $\theta_0,\dots,\theta_3$ for the core readings.  So the real
  total turn is $\theta_0+\dots+\theta_3=2\pi$, which is the second
  component of $N$.  For the first component, the four-edge closure gap is
  \[
    \operatorname{closureGap}=2\,u(\theta_0)\bigl(L_0+L_1u(\theta_1)
      +L_2u(\theta_1+\theta_2)+L_3u(\theta_1+\theta_2+\theta_3)\bigr)
  \]
  (\verb|closure_gap_four_unit_phase|): the factor $2$ converts
  half-lengths to lengths and $u(\theta_0)$ is the heading of the first edge.
  Since the gap is zero and $2u(\theta_0)\ne0$, the half-closure vanishes.
  Thus both components of the \emph{original} native controller vanish.

lean.code:
theorem repeatedMaximumCore_physical {p t h l u v : ℝ}
    (hp1 : p < 1) (ht1 : t < 1) (hh1 : h < 1) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (hu : u ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hv : v ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    NativeLengthPhysical p t 1 h l (orderedCoreHalfLengths u 1 v) := by
  have hd := r_core_realization_data zero_lt_one hu.1 zero_lt_one hv.1
    hu.2 hu.2 hv.2 hv.2
  have hs := r_core_sides_pos zero_lt_one hu.1 zero_lt_one hv.1 hu.2 hu.2 hv.2 hv.2
  have hm := moderateArc_zero_iff.mp hd.1
  have hw0 := (hm (0 : ZMod 4)).2
  have hw2 := (hm (2 : ZMod 4)).2
  change |(1 : ℝ)| * (rCoreSideD 1 u 1 v / 2) < 1 ∧
    |(1 : ℝ)| * (rCoreSideA 1 u 1 v / 2) < 1 at hw0
  change |(1 : ℝ)| * (rCoreSideB 1 u 1 v / 2) < 1 ∧
    |(1 : ℝ)| * (rCoreSideC 1 u 1 v / 2) < 1 at hw2
  simp only [abs_one, one_mul] at hw0 hw2
  refine ⟨?_, hw0.2, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, hw0.1⟩
  · intro i
    fin_cases i
    · exact half_pos hs.1
    · exact half_pos hs.2.1
    · exact half_pos hs.2.2.1
    · exact half_pos hs.2.2.2
  · exact (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hp1 (half_pos hs.1)).trans (by simpa using hw0.2)
  · exact (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right ht1 (half_pos hs.2.1)).trans (by simpa using hw2.1)
  · change 1 * (rCoreSideB 1 u 1 v / 2) < 1
    simpa only [one_mul] using hw2.1
  · change 1 * (rCoreSideC 1 u 1 v / 2) < 1
    simpa only [one_mul] using hw2.2
  · exact (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hh1 (half_pos hs.2.2.1)).trans (by simpa using hw2.2)
  · exact (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hl1 (half_pos hs.2.2.2)).trans (by simpa using hw0.1)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.exists_zero_of_two_crossed_corners
lean.code:
theorem exists_zero_of_two_crossed_corners
    {F G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ}
    (hF : ContinuousOn F (Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1))
    (hG : ContinuousOn G (Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1))
    (hleft : ∀ v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, 0 < F (0, v))
    (hbottom : ∀ u ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, 0 < G (u, 0))
    (hright : ∀ v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, G (1, v) = 0 → F (1, v) < 0)
    (htop : ∀ u ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, F (u, 1) = 0 → G (u, 1) < 0)
    (hcorner : G (1, 1) < 0) :
    ∃ z ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, F z = 0 ∧ G z = 0 := by
  let R : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ × ℝ := fun z =>
    (z.1 - clampUnit (z.1 + F z), z.2 - clampUnit (z.2 + G z))
  have hR : ContinuousOn R (Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1) := by
    dsimp [R, clampUnit]
    fun_prop
  obtain ⟨z, hz, hzero⟩ := poincare_miranda
    (a₁ := 0) (a₂ := 1) (b₁ := 0) (b₂ := 1) zero_le_one zero_le_one R hR
    (fun v _ => by dsimp [R]; simp only [zero_add]; linarith [(clampUnit_bounds (F (0, v))).1])
    (fun v _ => by dsimp [R]; linarith [(clampUnit_bounds (1 + F (1, v))).2])
    (fun u _ => by dsimp [R]; simp only [zero_add]; linarith [(clampUnit_bounds (G (u, 0))).1])
    (fun u _ => by dsimp [R]; linarith [(clampUnit_bounds (1 + G (u, 1))).2])
  have hf : clampUnit (z.1 + F z) = z.1 := by
    have := congrArg Prod.fst hzero
    change z.1 - clampUnit (z.1 + F z) = 0 at this
    linarith
  have hg : clampUnit (z.2 + G z) = z.2 := by
    have := congrArg Prod.snd hzero
    change z.2 - clampUnit (z.2 + G z) = 0 at this
    linarith
  have hu0 : 0 < z.1 := by
    by_contra hh
    have he : z.1 = 0 := le_antisymm (le_of_not_gt hh) hz.1.1
    have hc := clampUnit_eq_zero_le (he ▸ hf)
    have hp := hleft z.2 hz.2
    have hpair : z = (0, z.2) := Prod.ext he rfl
    rw [hpair] at hc
    simp only [zero_add] at hc
    linarith
  have hv0 : 0 < z.2 := by
    by_contra hh
    have he : z.2 = 0 := le_antisymm (le_of_not_gt hh) hz.2.1
    have hc := clampUnit_eq_zero_le (he ▸ hg)
    have hp := hbottom z.1 hz.1
    have hpair : z = (z.1, 0) := Prod.ext rfl he
    rw [hpair] at hc
    simp only [zero_add] at hc
    linarith
  have hu1 : z.1 < 1 := by
    by_contra hh
    have he : z.1 = 1 := le_antisymm hz.1.2 (le_of_not_gt hh)
    have hfge := one_le_of_clampUnit_eq_one (he ▸ hf)
    by_cases hev : z.2 = 1
    · have hgge := one_le_of_clampUnit_eq_one (hev ▸ hg)
      have hpair : z = (1, 1) := Prod.ext he hev
      rw [hpair] at hgge
      change 1 ≤ 1 + G (1, 1) at hgge
      linarith
    · have hv1 : z.2 < 1 := lt_of_le_of_ne hz.2.2 hev
      have hgz : G z = 0 := by
        have := eq_of_clampUnit_eq_interior hv0 hv1 hg
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
Conditions (2)--(3) are signs \emph{at boundary zeros} only; nothing is
  assumed about the sign of $F$ on the right edge or of $G$ on the top edge
  elsewhere.  Let $c(x)=\max(0,\min(1,x))$ be the clamp to $[0,1]$ and
  \[
    \mathcal G(u,v)=\bigl(u-c(u+F(u,v)),\ v-c(v+G(u,v))\bigr),
  \]
  continuous on $[0,1]^2$.  Since $c$ takes values in $[0,1]$,
  $\mathcal G_1(0,v)=-c(\cdot)\le0$, $\mathcal G_1(1,v)=1-c(\cdot)\ge0$, and
  likewise for $\mathcal G_2$ on the bottom and top.
  \Cref{lem:nrn_poincare_miranda_rect} gives $(u,v)\in[0,1]^2$ with
  $c(u+F)=u$ and $c(v+G)=v$.  We use three facts about the clamp:
  $c(x)=0\Rightarrow x\le0$; $c(x)=1\Rightarrow x\ge1$; and
  $c(x)=z\in(0,1)\Rightarrow x=z$.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $u>0$: if $u=0$ then $c(F(0,v))=0$, so $F(0,v)\le0$,
      contradicting (1).  Symmetrically $v>0$ by the bottom sign.
    \item $u<1$: if $u=1$ then $c(1+F(1,v))=1$, so $F(1,v)\ge0$.  If also
      $v=1$, then $c(1+G(1,1))=1$ gives $G(1,1)\ge0$, contradicting (4).  If
      $0<v<1$, the clamp in the second equation is inactive, so
      $v+G(1,v)=v$ and $G(1,v)=0$; by (2) $F(1,v)<0$, a contradiction.
    \item $v<1$: now $0<u<1$, so the first equation gives $F(u,v)=0$.  If
      $v=1$ then $F(u,1)=0$, so $G(u,1)<0$ by (3), while $c(1+G(u,1))=1$
      gives $G(u,1)\ge0$.
  \end{itemize}
  At the interior point both clamps are inactive, so $F(u,v)=G(u,v)=0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.rResidualOne_top_zero_iff
lean.code:
lemma rResidualOne_top_zero_iff {p t q u : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hq : 1 < q) (hu : u ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    rResidualOne p t q u 1 = 0 ↔ u = p := by
  let a := Real.sqrt (q ^ 2 - 1) / Real.sqrt (q ^ 2 - u ^ 2)
  have hnum : 0 < q ^ 2 - 1 := by nlinarith
  have hden : 0 < q ^ 2 - u ^ 2 := by nlinarith [hu.1, hu.2]
  have ha0 : 0 < a := div_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hnum) (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hden)
  have ha1 : a ≤ 1 := by
    apply (div_le_one (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hden)).2
    apply Real.sqrt_le_sqrt
    nlinarith [hu.1, hu.2]
  have hpaa : p * a ≤ 1 :=
    (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hp1.le ha0.le).trans (by simpa using ha1)
  have huaa : u * a ≤ 1 :=
    (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hu.2 ha0.le).trans (by simpa using ha1)
  have hexpr : rResidualOne p t q u 1 = Real.arcsin (p * a) - Real.arcsin (u * a) := by
    simp [rResidualOne, a]
  rw [hexpr, sub_eq_zero]
  constructor
  · intro he
    have heq := (Real.arcsin_inj (by nlinarith [mul_pos hp ha0] : -1 ≤ p * a) hpaa
      (by nlinarith [mul_nonneg hu.1 ha0.le] : -1 ≤ u * a) huaa).1 he
    nlinarith
  · intro he
    rw [he]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.rResidualOne_left_pos
lean.code:
lemma rResidualOne_left_pos {p t q v : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (ht : 0 < t)
    (hq : 1 < q) (hv : v ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : 0 < rResidualOne p t q 0 v := by
  have hrad : 0 < q ^ 2 - v ^ 2 := by nlinarith [hv.1, hv.2]
  have hden : 0 < Real.sqrt (q ^ 2) := Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by nlinarith)
  have ha := div_pos (Real.sqrt_pos.2 hrad) hden
  have hb : 0 ≤ Real.sqrt (1 - v ^ 2) / Real.sqrt (q ^ 2) := by positivity
  have hpa := Real.arcsin_pos.2 (mul_pos hp ha)
  have htb := Real.arcsin_nonneg.2 (mul_nonneg ht.le hb)
  simp only [rResidualOne, show (0 : ℝ) ^ 2 = 0 by norm_num,
    zero_mul, sub_zero, Real.arcsin_zero]
  linarith

blocks.tex:
(1) At $u=0$ we have $d=q$ and the two $u$-terms are $\arcsin0=0$, so
  $R_1(0,v)=\arcsin(p\sqrt{q^2-v^2}/q)+\arcsin(t\sqrt{1-v^2}/q)$.  The first
  argument is positive ($q^2-v^2>0$) and the second nonnegative.

  (2) At $v=1$ the $t$- and second $u$-terms vanish
  ($\sqrt{1-1}=0$) and
  \[
    R_1(u,1)=\arcsin(pa)-\arcsin(ua),\qquad
    a=\frac{\sqrt{q^2-1}}{\sqrt{q^2-u^2}}\in(0,1]
  \]
  (numerator $\le$ denominator since $u^2\le1$).  Both $pa$ and $ua$ lie in
  $[-1,1]$, where the principal arcsine is injective, so $R_1(u,1)=0$ iff
  $pa=ua$ iff $u=p$ ($a>0$).  This is an exact comparison; the zero is not
  located numerically.

  (3) The first identity is \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_faces}(5)
  (\verb|r_corner_eq_firstPairFlag|: at $(1,l)$ the $A$-scale is $1$ and the
  $B$-scale is $\sigma(q,l)$).  By \cref{lem:nrn_residual_basics},
  $R_3(p,1)=\operatorname{R}_1(l,h,q;1,p)$, which by the same identity with
  $(p,t,l)$ replaced by $(l,h,p)$ is $\Phi(l,h,q,p)$.

  (4) This is \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_faces}(1) at $v=1$
  (\verb|r_residual_three_right_neg|, which needs only $0\le l<v\le1<q$).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.exists_r_zero_of_negative_corners
lean.code:
theorem exists_r_zero_of_negative_corners {p t q h l : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (hh : 0 < h) (hq : 1 < q)
    (hflag : firstPairFlag p t q l < 0)
    (hreflected : firstPairFlag l h q p < 0) :
    ∃ z ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, rResidualMap p t q h l z = 0 := by
  have hden : ∀ z ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      0 < q ^ 2 - z.1 ^ 2 * z.2 ^ 2 :=
    fun z hz => r_denom_pos_aux hq hz.1.1 hz.1.2 hz.2.1 hz.2.2
  obtain ⟨z, hz, hF, hG⟩ := exists_zero_of_two_crossed_corners
    (continuousOn_rResidualOne_of_denom_pos (p := p) (t := t) hden)
    (continuousOn_rResidualThree_of_denom_pos (h := h) (l := l) hden)
    (fun v hv => rResidualOne_left_pos hp ht hq hv)
    (fun u hu => by rw [rResidualThree_eq_swap]; exact rResidualOne_left_pos hl hh hq hu)
    (fun v hv hG => by
      rw [rResidualThree_eq_swap] at hG
      have he := (rResidualOne_top_zero_iff hl hl1 hq hv).1 hG
      rw [he, r_corner_eq_firstPairFlag hl hl1 hq]
      exact hflag)
    (fun u hu hF => by
      have he := (rResidualOne_top_zero_iff hp hp1 hq hu).1 hF
      rw [he, rResidualThree_eq_swap, r_corner_eq_firstPairFlag hp hp1 hq]
      exact hreflected)
    (r_residual_three_right_neg hl.le hl1 le_rfl hq)
  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
  apply Complex.ext
  · simpa only [r_residual_map_re, Complex.zero_re] using hF
  · simpa only [r_residual_map_im, Complex.zero_im] using hG

blocks.tex:
On the closed square $u^2v^2\le1<q^2$, so $q^2-u^2v^2>0$
  (\verb|r_denom_pos_aux|, \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_walls}) and $F=R_1$,
  $G=R_3$ are continuous on $[0,1]^2$ (\cref{lem:nrn_residual_basics}).
  We check the hypotheses of \cref{lem:nrn_crossed_square}.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Left: $F(0,v)>0$ by \cref{lem:nrn_negative_faces}(1).
      Bottom: $G(u,0)=\operatorname{R}_1(l,h,q;0,u)>0$ by reflection and
      the same statement for $(l,h)$.
    \item Right-edge zeros: $G(1,v)=\operatorname{R}_1(l,h,q;v,1)$, which by
      \cref{lem:nrn_negative_faces}(2) (for $l$) vanishes iff $v=l$.  There
      $F(1,l)=\Phi(p,t,q,l)<0$ by \cref{lem:nrn_negative_faces}(3).
    \item Top-edge zeros: $F(u,1)=0$ iff $u=p$, and then
      $G(p,1)=\Phi(l,h,q,p)<0$.
    \item Corner: $G(1,1)<0$ by \cref{lem:nrn_negative_faces}(4).
  \end{itemize}
  The lemma gives $(u,v)\in(0,1)^2$ with $R_1=R_3=0$, i.e.\
  $\mathcal R(u,v)=0$.  The two flags enter only at the two boundary zeros;
  no uniqueness of a scalar root and no replacement of the target readings
  by effective ones is used.

blocks.label: lem:nrn_negative_physical
blocks.title: all eight walls on a negative-corner core
blocks.body:
Let $0<p<1$, $0<l<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<h<q$, $q>1$ and $u,v\in(0,1)$.  Then
  $L^{\mathrm{core}}(u,v)$ is physical for $(p,t,q,h,l)$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.negativeCornersCore_physical
lean.code:
theorem negativeCornersCore_physical {p t q h l u v : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (_hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (_ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (_hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (hq : 1 < q) (hu : u ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hv : v ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    NativeLengthPhysical p t q h l (orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v) := by
  have hd := r_core_realization_data (q := q) zero_lt_one hu.1 (by linarith) hv.1
    hu.2 (by linarith [hu.2]) hv.2 (by linarith [hv.2])
  have hs := r_core_sides_pos zero_lt_one hu.1 (by linarith : 0 < q) hv.1
    hu.2 (by linarith [hu.2]) hv.2 (by linarith [hv.2])
  have hm := moderateArc_zero_iff.mp hd.1
  have hw0 := (hm (0 : ZMod 4)).2
  have hw2 := (hm (2 : ZMod 4)).2
  change |(1 : ℝ)| * (rCoreSideD 1 u q v / 2) < 1 ∧
    |(1 : ℝ)| * (rCoreSideA 1 u q v / 2) < 1 at hw0
  change |q| * (rCoreSideB 1 u q v / 2) < 1 ∧
    |q| * (rCoreSideC 1 u q v / 2) < 1 at hw2
  simp only [abs_one, one_mul] at hw0
  rw [abs_of_pos (by linarith : 0 < q)] at hw2
  refine ⟨?_, hw0.2, ?_, ?_, hw2.1, hw2.2, ?_, ?_, hw0.1⟩
  · intro i
    fin_cases i
    · exact half_pos hs.1
    · exact half_pos hs.2.1
    · exact half_pos hs.2.2.1
    · exact half_pos hs.2.2.2
  · exact (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hp1 (half_pos hs.1)).trans (by simpa using hw0.2)
  · exact (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right htq (half_pos hs.2.1)).trans hw2.1
  · exact (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hhq (half_pos hs.2.2.1)).trans hw2.2
  · exact (mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hl1 (half_pos hs.2.2.2)).trans (by simpa using hw0.1)

blocks.tex:
Positivity is \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_core}.  Its strict moderate-arc walls
  at vertex $0$ (curvature $1$) give $L_3<1$, $L_0<1$, and at vertex $2$
  (curvature $q$) give $qL_1<1$, $qL_2<1$: these are the four pure walls.
  Then $pL_0<L_0<1$ and $lL_3<L_3<1$ because $p,l<1$, and
  $tL_1<qL_1<1$, $hL_2<qL_2<1$ because $t,h<q$.  No relation between the
  core readings $u,v$ and the actual readings $p,t,h,l$ is needed; this is
  why the ordered-branch physicality statement of
  \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_native_zero}, which uses $p<u$, $l<v$ and
  $\mathrm{(HB)}$, is not used here.

blocks.label: thm:nrn_negative_zero
blocks.title: a physical negative-corner native zero
blocks.body:
Let $0<p<1$, $0<l<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<h<q$, $q>1$, $\Phi(p,t,q,l)<0$ and
  $\Phi(l,h,q,p)<0$.  Then there are $u,v\in(0,1)$ such that
  $L=L^{\mathrm{core}}(u,v)$ is physical for $(p,t,q,h,l)$,
  $\mathcal R(u,v)=0$ and $N(L)=0$.

theorem exists_nativeLength_anchor_of_negative_corners {p t q h l : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q) (hq : 1 < q)
    (hflag : firstPairFlag p t q l < 0)
    (hreflected : firstPairFlag l h q p < 0) :
    ∃ u v : ℝ, u ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ v ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
      NativeLengthPhysical p t q h l (orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v) ∧
      rResidualMap p t q h l (u, v) = 0 ∧
      nativeLengthController p t q h l (orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨z, hz, hzero⟩ := exists_r_zero_of_negative_corners hp hp1 hl hl1 ht hh hq hflag hreflected
  exact ⟨z.1, z.2, hz.1, hz.2,
    negativeCornersCore_physical hp hp1 hl hl1 ht htq hh hhq hq hz.1 hz.2,
    hzero, native_zero_of_ordered_r_zero hz.1.1 hz.2.1 hq hz.1.2 hz.2.2 hzero⟩

Take the zero of \cref{thm:nrn_negative_root}.  Physicality is
  \cref{lem:nrn_negative_physical}.  The native zero is the zero part of
  \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_native_zero} (\verb|native_zero_of_ordered_r_zero|),
  whose hypotheses are only $0<u,v<1<q$ and $\mathcal R(u,v)=0$: the
  argument is the slot-by-slot turn comparison and the core closure of
  \cref{lem:nrn_repeated_native_zero}, now with core curvature $q$.

blocks.title: Incident rank: the nonacute chamber

blocks.tex:
In this section and the next the hypotheses are
\[
  0<p<1,\quad 0<l<1,\quad 0<t<q,\quad 0<h<q,\quad q\ge1,
\]
and $L$ is a physical native zero.  By \cref{lem:nfp_split_lengths}(3) write
$L=(\sin\alpha,\sin\gamma/q,\sin\delta/q,\sin\beta)$ with strict angles and
put $S=\alpha+\beta$, $T=\gamma+\delta$.  In this chapter the letters
$A,B,C,D$ denote \emph{defect slopes}
\[
  A=1-\operatorname{slope}(p,\alpha),\quad
  B=1-\operatorname{slope}(l,\beta),\quad
  C=1-\operatorname{slope}(t/q,\gamma),\quad
  D=1-\operatorname{slope}(h/q,\delta),
\]
all in $(0,1)$ by \cref{lem:nfp_angle_slopes} since all four coefficients
$p,l,t/q,h/q$ lie in $(0,1)$.  (The turn defect of
\cref{def:nfp_split_model} is referred to in words.)  The first-transition
rank theorem \cref{thm:nfp_native_rank} is \emph{not} available: its
fourth coefficient $h/q$ exceeds one.

blocks.label: lem:nrn_incident_obtuse
blocks.title: the first pure turn is obtuse for $q\ge1$
blocks.body:
Let $0<p<1$, $0<t<q$, $q>0$, $\alpha,\gamma\in(0,\pi/2)$ and low seam
  $H=0$.  Then $S+T>\pi$.  If moreover $\beta,\delta\in(0,\pi/2)$, $q\ge1$
  and the chord vanishes, $\sin S=\sin T/q$, then $\pi/2<S<\pi$ and
  $\cos S<0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.angle_sums_gt_pi_of_seamLow_zero
lean.code:
theorem angle_sums_gt_pi_of_seamLow_zero {p t q α β γ δ : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hα : α ∈ Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2)) (hγ : γ ∈ Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2))
    (hlow : seamLow p t q α β γ δ = 0) :
    Real.pi < (α + β) + (γ + δ) := by
  have hpa := endpointAtom_lt_angle hp hp1 hα.1 hα.2
  have htg := endpointAtom_lt_angle (div_pos ht hq) ((div_lt_one hq).2 htq)
    hγ.1 hγ.2
  unfold seamLow lowTurn angleAtom at hlow
  linarith

blocks.tex:
$H=0$ says $S+T-\pi=(\alpha-\operatorname{atom}(p,\alpha))+
  (\gamma-\operatorname{atom}(t/q,\gamma))$, a sum of two positive deficits
  (\cref{lem:nfp_angle_slopes}, $p<1$, $t/q<1$).  For the second claim
  $S,T\in(0,\pi)$.  If $S\le\pi/2$, then $-\pi/2\le\pi-T<S\le\pi/2$ and the
  sine is increasing there, so $\sin T=\sin(\pi-T)<\sin S$.  But
  $\sin S>0$ and $q\ge1$ give $\sin T=q\sin S\ge\sin S$.  Hence $S>\pi/2$
  and $\cos S<0$.  (The case $q=1$ is included; this is the private helper
  \verb|cos_first_sum_neg_of_one_le| used inside
  \cref{lem:nrn_incident_split_rank}.)

blocks.label: def:nrn_incident_chart
blocks.title: the incident chart
blocks.body:
Fix $\gamma$.  In coordinates $x=(S,\alpha,T)\in\RR^3$ put
  $\beta=S-\alpha$, $\delta=T-\gamma$ and
  \[
    \Sigma_\gamma(x)=(M,H,K),\qquad
    \mathcal N_\gamma(x)=(E,\text{turn defect}),\qquad
    \ell_\gamma(x)=\bigl(\sin\alpha,\ \sin\gamma/q,\ \sin(T-\gamma)/q,\
      \sin(S-\alpha)\bigr),
  \]
  the chord, low seam and high seam, the split half-closure and turn
  defect of \cref{def:nfp_split_model}, and the half-lengths
  (\verb|incidentSplitController|, \verb|incidentNativeController|,
  \verb|incidentHalfLengths|).

blocks.tex:
The chart of \cref{lem:nfp_split_rank} fixed $T$ and varied $\gamma$; here
$\gamma$ is fixed and $T$ varies.  Consequently the chord $M=\sin S-\sin T/q$
depends on two coordinates, and the closure coefficient $\sin T/q$ is not
constant.

blocks.label: lem:nrn_incident_differential
blocks.title: derivative of the incident chart
blocks.body:
Let $0<p<1$, $0<l<1$, $0<h<q$ and let the angles at $x$ be strict.  With
  $R=\cos S$ and $W=\cos T/q$, $\Sigma_\gamma$ has derivative at $x$
  \[
    J=\begin{pmatrix}R&0&-W\\ 1&-A&1\\ 1-B&B&1-D\end{pmatrix}
    \qquad(\text{\texttt{incidentDifferential R W A B D}}),
  \]
  and, with $U=A+B-AB$ and $V=A+B-AD$,
  \[
    -\det J=R\,V+W\,U=R\,(A+B-AD)+W\,(A+B-AB).
  \]
  $J$ is surjective whenever $A\ne0$ and $RV+WU\ne0$.  In particular it is
  surjective if $R<0$, $W\le0$, $0<A<1$, $B>0$ and $D<1$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.incidentDifferential_surjective_of_det_ne_zero
lean.code:
theorem incidentDifferential_surjective_of_det_ne_zero {R W A B D : ℝ}
    (hA : A ≠ 0)
    (hdet : R * (A + B - A * D) + W * (A + B - A * B) ≠ 0) :
    Function.Surjective (incidentDifferential R W A B D) := by
  let U := A + B - A * B
  let V := A + B - A * D
  intro y
  let N := A * y 2 + B * y 1
  let S := (V * y 0 + W * N) / (R * V + W * U)
  let T := (R * N - U * y 0) / (R * V + W * U)
  have hdet' : R * V + W * U ≠ 0 := hdet
  have hm : R * S - W * T = y 0 := by
    dsimp [S, T]
    field_simp [hdet']
    ring
  have hn : U * S + V * T = N := by
    calc
      _ = (R * V + W * U) * N / (R * V + W * U) := by
        dsimp [S, T]
        ring
      _ = N := mul_div_cancel_left₀ N hdet
  refine ⟨![S, (S + T - y 1) / A, T], ?_⟩
  ext i
  fin_cases i
  · simpa [incidentDifferential] using hm
  · simp [incidentDifferential]
    field_simp
    ring
  · change (1 - B) * S + B * ((S + T - y 1) / A) + (1 - D) * T = y 2
    apply (mul_left_inj' hA).mp
    have hcancel : A * ((S + T - y 1) / A) = S + T - y 1 :=
      mul_div_cancel₀ _ hA
    dsimp [U, V, N] at hn
    linear_combination hn + B * hcancel

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.incidentDifferential
lean.code:
noncomputable def incidentDifferential (R W A B D : ℝ) :
    (Fin 3 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (Fin 3 → ℝ) :=
  ContinuousLinearMap.pi ![
    R • ContinuousLinearMap.proj 0 - W • ContinuousLinearMap.proj 2,
    ContinuousLinearMap.proj 0 - A • ContinuousLinearMap.proj 1 +
      ContinuousLinearMap.proj 2,
    (1 - B) • ContinuousLinearMap.proj 0 + B • ContinuousLinearMap.proj 1 +
      (1 - D) • ContinuousLinearMap.proj 2]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.incidentDifferential_surjective
lean.code:
theorem incidentDifferential_surjective {R W A B D : ℝ}
    (hR : R < 0) (hW : W ≤ 0) (hA : 0 < A) (hA1 : A < 1)
    (hB : 0 < B) (hD1 : D < 1) :
    Function.Surjective (incidentDifferential R W A B D) := by
  let U := A + B - A * B
  let V := A + B - A * D
  have hU : 0 < U := by
    dsimp [U]
    nlinarith [mul_pos hB (sub_pos.mpr hA1)]
  have hV : 0 < V := by
    dsimp [V]
    nlinarith [mul_pos hA (sub_pos.mpr hD1)]
  have hdet : R * V + W * U ≠ 0 :=
    ne_of_lt (add_neg_of_neg_of_nonpos (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos hR hV)
      (mul_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg hW hU.le))
  intro y
  let N := A * y 2 + B * y 1
  let S := (V * y 0 + W * N) / (R * V + W * U)
  let T := (R * N - U * y 0) / (R * V + W * U)
  have hm : R * S - W * T = y 0 := by
    dsimp [S, T]
    field_simp
    ring
  have hn : U * S + V * T = N := by
    calc
      _ = (R * V + W * U) * N / (R * V + W * U) := by
        dsimp [S, T]
        ring
      _ = N := mul_div_cancel_left₀ N hdet
  refine ⟨![S, (S + T - y 1) / A, T], ?_⟩
  ext i
  fin_cases i
  · simpa [incidentDifferential] using hm
  · simp [incidentDifferential]
    field_simp
    ring
  · simp [incidentDifferential]
    apply (mul_left_inj' (ne_of_gt hA)).mp
    have hcancel : A * ((S + T - y 1) / A) = S + T - y 1 :=
      mul_div_cancel₀ _ (ne_of_gt hA)
    dsimp [U, V, N] at hn
    nlinarith

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.hasFDerivAt_incidentSplitController
lean.code:
theorem hasFDerivAt_incidentSplitController
    {p t q h l γ : ℝ} {x : Fin 3 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q) (hq : 0 < q)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) γ (x 2 - γ)) :
    HasFDerivAt (incidentSplitController p t q h l γ)
      (incidentDifferential (Real.cos (x 0)) (Real.cos (x 2) / q)
        (1 - angleSlope p (x 1)) (1 - angleSlope l (x 0 - x 1))
        (1 - angleSlope (h / q) (x 2 - γ))) x := by
  have h0 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 0 x
  have h1 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 1 x
  have h2 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 2 x
  have hpD := (hasDerivAt_angleDefect hp hp1 ha.1.1 ha.1.2).comp_hasFDerivAt x h1
  have hlD := (hasDerivAt_angleDefect hl hl1 ha.2.1.1 ha.2.1.2).comp_hasFDerivAt x
    (h0.sub h1)
  have hhD := (hasDerivAt_angleDefect (div_pos hh hq) ((div_lt_one hq).mpr hhq)
    ha.2.2.2.1.1 ha.2.2.2.1.2).comp_hasFDerivAt x (h2.sub_const γ)
  have hM := ((Real.hasDerivAt_sin (x 0)).comp_hasFDerivAt x h0).sub
    (((Real.hasDerivAt_sin (x 2)).comp_hasFDerivAt x h2).mul_const q⁻¹)
  have hH := ((((h0.add h2).sub_const Real.pi).sub hpD).sub_const
    (angleDefect (t / q) γ))
  have hK := (((h0.add h2).sub_const Real.pi).sub hlD).sub hhD
  apply hasFDerivAt_pi.mpr
  intro i
  fin_cases i
  · convert hM using 1
    · ext z
      simp [incidentSplitController, chord, Function.comp_def, div_eq_mul_inv]
    · ext z
      simp [div_eq_mul_inv]
      ring
  · convert hH using 1
    · ext z
      simp [incidentSplitController, seamLow, lowTurn, angleDefect, Function.comp_def]
      ring
    · ext z
      simp
      ring
  · convert hK using 1
    · ext z
      simp [incidentSplitController, seamHigh, highTurn, angleDefect, Function.comp_def]
      ring
    · ext z
      simp
      ring

blocks.tex:
\emph{Derivative.}  $M=\sin S-\sin T/q$ has gradient $(\cos S,0,-\cos T/q)$.
  With the deficits $\operatorname{def}(a,z)=z-\operatorname{atom}(a,z)$
  (\verb|angleDefect|),
  \[
    H=S+T-\pi-\operatorname{def}(p,\alpha)-\operatorname{def}(t/q,\gamma),
    \qquad
    K=S+T-\pi-\operatorname{def}(l,S-\alpha)-\operatorname{def}(h/q,T-\gamma).
  \]
  The term $\operatorname{def}(t/q,\gamma)$ is constant.  By
  \cref{lem:nfp_angle_slopes} each deficit has derivative
  $1-\operatorname{slope}$ at an acute angle (for $h/q<1$ no high wall is
  needed).  So $H$ has gradient $(1,-A,1)$, and $K$ has gradient
  $(1-B,\,B,\,1-D)$ because $\partial\beta/\partial S=1$,
  $\partial\beta/\partial\alpha=-1$ and $\partial\delta/\partial T=1$.

  \emph{Determinant.}  Expanding along the first row,
  $\det J=R(-A(1-D)-B)-W(B+A(1-B))=-(RV+WU)$.

  \emph{Explicit preimage.}  Given $y$, put $N=Ay_2+By_1$ and solve the
  $2\times2$ system
  \[
    R\,S'-W\,T'=y_0,\qquad U\,S'+V\,T'=N
  \]
  by Cramer's rule: $S'=(Vy_0+WN)/(RV+WU)$, $T'=(RN-Uy_0)/(RV+WU)$.  Put
  $\alpha'=(S'+T'-y_1)/A$.  Then row $1$ gives $S'-A\alpha'+T'=y_1$, and
  row $2$ multiplied by $A$ is
  $A(1-B)S'+B(S'+T'-y_1)+A(1-D)T'=US'+VT'-By_1=Ay_2$.  So
  $J(S',\alpha',T')=y$.

  \emph{Signs.}  $U=A+B(1-A)>0$ when $0<A<1$ and $B>0$, and
  $V=A(1-D)+B>0$ when $A>0$, $D<1$ and $B>0$.  Then
  $RV<0$ and $WU\le0$, so $RV+WU<0$.

lean.code:
theorem fderiv_incidentSplitController_surjective
    {p t q h l γ : ℝ} {x : Fin 3 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q)
    (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hT : Real.pi / 2 ≤ x 2)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) γ (x 2 - γ))
    (hzero : incidentSplitController p t q h l γ x = 0) :
    Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (incidentSplitController p t q h l γ) x) := by
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  have hlow : seamLow p t q (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) γ (x 2 - γ) = 0 :=
    congrFun hzero 1
  have hchord : chord q (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) γ (x 2 - γ) = 0 :=
    congrFun hzero 0
  have hsum := angle_sums_gt_pi_of_seamLow_zero hp hp1 ht htq hq0 ha.1 ha.2.2.1 hlow
  have hR : Real.cos (x 0) < 0 := by
    apply cos_first_sum_neg_of_one_le (q := q) (T := x 2)
      (by linarith [ha.1.1, ha.2.1.1]) (by linarith [ha.1.2, ha.2.1.2])
      (by linarith [ha.2.2.1.2, ha.2.2.2.1.2]) (by linarith) hq
    simpa [chord] using sub_eq_zero.mp hchord
  have hW : Real.cos (x 2) / q ≤ 0 := by
    apply div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg _ hq0.le
    exact Real.cos_nonpos_of_pi_div_two_le_of_le hT
      (by linarith [ha.2.2.1.2, ha.2.2.2.1.2, Real.pi_pos])
  rw [(hasFDerivAt_incidentSplitController hp hp1 hl hl1 hh hhq hq0 ha).fderiv]
  exact incidentDifferential_surjective hR hW
    (lowDefect_derivative_pos hp hp1 ha.1.1 ha.1.2)
    (by
      have hs := angleSlope_pos hp ha.1.1 ha.1.2
        (endpoint_arg_lt_one hp hp1 ha.1.1 ha.1.2)
      linarith)
    (lowDefect_derivative_pos hl hl1 ha.2.1.1 ha.2.1.2)
    (by
      have hs := angleSlope_pos (div_pos hh hq0) ha.2.2.2.1.1 ha.2.2.2.1.2
        (endpoint_arg_lt_one (div_pos hh hq0) ((div_lt_one hq0).mpr hhq)
          ha.2.2.2.1.1 ha.2.2.2.1.2)
      linarith)

  $\pi/2\le T<\pi$, $W=\cos T/q\le0$ (equality at $T=\pi/2$ is allowed).

blocks.label: lem:nrn_incident_transfer
blocks.title: transfer to the actual closure and turn
blocks.body:
Let $\Sigma_\gamma$ have derivative $J'$ at a zero $x$.  Then
  $\mathcal N_\gamma$ has derivative $\Lambda\circ J'$ at $x$, where
  \[
    \Lambda(dM,dH,dK)=\bigl(u(-\beta)(dM-i\varrho\,dH)+c\,(dH+dK),\ dH+dK\bigr),
    \qquad \varrho=\frac{\sin T}q,\quad c=i\sin\beta\,u(-S),
  \]
  (\verb|closureTargetLinearMap|).  If $\varrho\ne0$, $\Lambda$ is bijective.
  Consequently, under the hypotheses of \cref{lem:nrn_incident_split_rank}
  with $\mathcal N_\gamma(x)=0$ in place of $\Sigma_\gamma(x)=0$,
  $D\mathcal N_\gamma(x)$ is surjective onto $\CC\times\RR$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.hasFDerivAt_incidentNativeController_of_split
lean.code:
theorem hasFDerivAt_incidentNativeController_of_split
    {p t q h l γ : ℝ} {x : Fin 3 → ℝ}
    {f' : (Fin 3 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] (Fin 3 → ℝ)}
    (hf : HasFDerivAt (incidentSplitController p t q h l γ) f' x)
    (hz : incidentSplitController p t q h l γ x = 0) :
    HasFDerivAt (incidentNativeController p t q h l γ)
      ((closureTargetLinearMap (x 0 - x 1) (Real.sin (x 2) / q)
        (Complex.I * (Real.sin (x 0 - x 1) : ℂ) *
          unitPhase (-(x 0)))).toContinuousLinearMap.comp f')
      x := by
  let f := incidentSplitController p t q h l γ
  have h0 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 0 x
  have h1 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 1 x
  have h2 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 2 x
  have hM := (ContinuousLinearMap.proj (R := ℝ) (φ := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 0).hasFDerivAt.comp x hf
  have hH := (ContinuousLinearMap.proj (R := ℝ) (φ := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 1).hasFDerivAt.comp x hf
  have hK := (ContinuousLinearMap.proj (R := ℝ) (φ := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 2).hasFDerivAt.comp x hf
  have hMC := Complex.ofRealCLM.hasFDerivAt.comp x hM
  have hphase := hasFDerivAt_incidentPhase (h0.sub h1).neg
  have hLow := hasFDerivAt_incidentPhase hH
  have hTurn := hasFDerivAt_incidentPhase (hH.add hK)
  have hsin := (Real.hasDerivAt_sin (x 0 - x 1)).comp_hasFDerivAt x (h0.sub h1)
  have hsinC := Complex.ofRealCLM.hasFDerivAt.comp x hsin
  have hcoeff := hsinC.mul (hasFDerivAt_incidentPhase h0.neg)
  have hr := ((Real.hasDerivAt_sin (x 2)).comp_hasFDerivAt x h2).mul_const q⁻¹
  have hrC := Complex.ofRealCLM.hasFDerivAt.comp x hr
  have hE := (hphase.mul (hMC.add (hrC.mul (hLow.const_sub 1)))).add
    (hcoeff.mul (hTurn.sub_const 1))
  have hprod := hE.prodMk (hH.add hK)
  have hfun : (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ =>
      (unitPhase (-(z 0 - z 1)) *
          ((f z 0 : ℂ) + ((Real.sin (z 2) * q⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) * (1 - unitPhase (f z 1))) +
        (Real.sin (z 0 - z 1) : ℂ) * unitPhase (-(z 0)) *
          (unitPhase (f z 1 + f z 2) - 1), f z 1 + f z 2)) =
      incidentNativeController p t q h l γ := by
    funext z
    apply Prod.ext
    · simp only [incidentNativeController, nativeHalfClosure_eq]
      have ht := seamLow_add_seamHigh p t q h l (z 1) (z 0 - z 1) γ (z 2 - γ)
      simp only [f, incidentSplitController, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
        Matrix.cons_val, chord]
      rw [ht]
      simp only [add_sub_cancel]
      simp only [div_eq_mul_inv]
      push_cast
      ring
    · exact seamLow_add_seamHigh p t q h l (z 1) (z 0 - z 1) γ (z 2 - γ)
  change HasFDerivAt (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ =>
      (unitPhase (-(z 0 - z 1)) *
          ((f z 0 : ℂ) + ((Real.sin (z 2) * q⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) * (1 - unitPhase (f z 1))) +
        (Real.sin (z 0 - z 1) : ℂ) * unitPhase (-(z 0)) *
          (unitPhase (f z 1 + f z 2) - 1), f z 1 + f z 2)) _ x at hprod
  rw [hfun] at hprod
  apply hprod.congr_fderiv
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro v
  apply Prod.ext
  · simp [closureTargetLinearMap, Function.comp_def, hz, unitPhase, div_eq_mul_inv]
    ring
  · simp [closureTargetLinearMap]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.fderiv_incidentNativeController_surjective
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_incidentNativeController_surjective
    {p t q h l γ : ℝ} {x : Fin 3 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q)
    (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hT : Real.pi / 2 ≤ x 2)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) γ (x 2 - γ))
    (hzero : incidentNativeController p t q h l γ x = 0) :
    Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (incidentNativeController p t q h l γ) x) := by
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  have hz := (native_zero_iff_of_strictAngles (l := l) hp.le ht.le hq0 ha).mp
    ⟨congrArg Prod.fst hzero, congrArg Prod.snd hzero⟩
  have hs : incidentSplitController p t q h l γ x = 0 := by
    ext i
    fin_cases i
    · exact hz.1
    · exact hz.2.1
    · exact hz.2.2
  have hf := hasFDerivAt_incidentSplitController (t := t) hp hp1 hl hl1 hh hhq hq0 ha
  have hn := hasFDerivAt_incidentNativeController_of_split hf hs
  have hsin : 0 < Real.sin (x 2) := Real.sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi
    (by linarith [ha.2.2.1.1, ha.2.2.2.1.1])
    (by linarith [ha.2.2.1.2, ha.2.2.2.1.2])
  rw [hn.fderiv]
  have htarget := closureTargetLinearMap_surjective
    (β := x 0 - x 1) (ne_of_gt (div_pos hsin hq0))
    (Complex.I * (Real.sin (x 0 - x 1) : ℂ) * unitPhase (-(x 0)))
  have hsplit := fderiv_incidentSplitController_surjective hp hp1 ht htq hl hl1
    hh hhq hq hT ha hs
  rw [hf.fderiv] at hsplit
  exact htarget.comp hsplit

blocks.tex:
\emph{Identity off the zero set.}  The closure identity (CI) of
  \cref{lem:nfp_native_equations} holds for all angles.  Writing
  $\sin(\alpha+\beta)=M+\sin T/q$ and using $H+K=$ turn defect
  (\verb|seamLow_add_seamHigh|), it becomes the identity of functions of $x$
  \[
    \mathcal N_\gamma(x)=\Bigl(u(-\beta)\bigl(M+\varrho(x)(1-u(H))\bigr)
      +\sin\beta\,u(-S)\bigl(u(H+K)-1\bigr),\ H+K\Bigr),
    \qquad \varrho(x)=\frac{\sin T}q .
  \]
  \emph{Differentiation at the zero.}  At $x$ we have $M=H=K=0$.  The factor
  $u(-\beta)$ multiplies $M+\varrho(1-u(H))=0$ and $\sin\beta\,u(-S)$
  multiplies $u(H+K)-1=0$, so their derivatives do not contribute.  In this
  chart $\varrho$ is \emph{not} constant ($T$ is a coordinate), but its
  derivative is multiplied by $1-u(H)=0$ and drops out as well.  What
  remains is $d\,u(H)=i\,dH$ and $d\,u(H+K)=i(dH+dK)$, which gives
  $\Lambda\circ J'$; the full-turn correction produces the $c$-term.  This
  is a derivative computation for the original map, not a comparison of
  zero sets.

  \emph{Bijectivity of $\Lambda$.}  If $dH+dK=0$ then
  $u(-\beta)(dM-i\varrho\,dH)=0$, so $dM=0$ and $dH=0=dK$.  Explicitly, a
  preimage of $(z,s)$ is $(\Re w,-\Im w/\varrho,s+\Im w/\varrho)$ with
  $w=u(\beta)(z-cs)$ (\verb|closureTargetLinearMap_surjective|).

  \emph{Rank.}  By \cref{lem:nfp_native_equations} ($p,t\ge0$, $q>0$,
  strict angles) the native zero is a zero of $\Sigma_\gamma$.  Here
  $T\in(0,\pi)$ gives $\varrho=\sin T/q>0$, and $D\Sigma_\gamma(x)$ is
  surjective by \cref{lem:nrn_incident_split_rank}; compose.  The hypotheses
  are the incident ones ($h<q$); no statement assuming $h>q$ is used.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.differentiableAt_nativeLengthController_of_physical
lean.code:
theorem differentiableAt_nativeLengthController_of_physical
    {p t q h l : ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (ht : 0 < t) (hq : 0 < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hl : 0 < l)
    (hphys : NativeLengthPhysical p t q h l L) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (nativeLengthController p t q h l) L := by
  rcases hphys with ⟨hpos, h0, hp0, ht1, hq1, hq2, hh2, hl3, h3⟩
  have hd {g : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → ℝ} (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g L)
      (hlo : 0 < g L) (hhi : g L < 1) :
      DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun z => Real.arcsin (g z)) L :=
    (Real.differentiableAt_arcsin.mpr ⟨by linarith, ne_of_lt hhi⟩).comp L hg
  have hd0 := hd (g := fun z => z 0) (by fun_prop) (hpos 0) h0
  have hd3 := hd (g := fun z => z 3) (by fun_prop) (hpos 3) h3
  have hdp := hd (g := fun z => p * z 0) (by fun_prop) (mul_pos hp (hpos 0)) hp0
  have hdt := hd (g := fun z => t * z 1) (by fun_prop) (mul_pos ht (hpos 1)) ht1
  have hdq1 := hd (g := fun z => q * z 1) (by fun_prop) (mul_pos hq (hpos 1)) hq1
  have hdq2 := hd (g := fun z => q * z 2) (by fun_prop) (mul_pos hq (hpos 2)) hq2
  have hdh := hd (g := fun z => h * z 2) (by fun_prop) (mul_pos hh (hpos 2)) hh2
  have hdl := hd (g := fun z => l * z 3) (by fun_prop) (mul_pos hl (hpos 3)) hl3
  unfold nativeLengthController lengthTurns unitPhase
  dsimp only [Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one, Matrix.cons_val,
    Matrix.head_cons, Matrix.head_fin_const]
  fun_prop

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_incident_angles
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_incident_angles
    {p t q h l γ : ℝ} {x : Fin 3 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q)
    (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hT : Real.pi / 2 ≤ x 2)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) γ (x 2 - γ))
    (hzero : incidentNativeController p t q h l γ x = 0) :
    Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeLengthController p t q h l)
      (incidentHalfLengths q γ x)) := by
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  have hphys : NativeLengthPhysical p t q h l (incidentHalfLengths q γ x) :=
    nativeLengthPhysical_splitHalfLengths hp hp1 ht htq hl hl1 hq0 ha
  have hd := differentiableAt_nativeLengthController_of_physical hp ht hq0 hh hl hphys
  have hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ (incidentHalfLengths q γ) x := by
    apply differentiableAt_pi.mpr
    intro i
    fin_cases i <;> dsimp [incidentHalfLengths, splitHalfLengths] <;> fun_prop
  have hc0 : ContinuousAt (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ => z 0) x := (continuous_apply 0).continuousAt
  have hc1 : ContinuousAt (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ => z 1) x := (continuous_apply 1).continuousAt
  have hc2 : ContinuousAt (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ => z 2) x := (continuous_apply 2).continuousAt
  have heα := hc1.eventually (Ioo_mem_nhds ha.1.1 ha.1.2)
  have heβ := (hc0.sub hc1).eventually (Ioo_mem_nhds ha.2.1.1 ha.2.1.2)
  have heδ := (hc2.sub_const γ).eventually
    (Ioo_mem_nhds ha.2.2.2.1.1 ha.2.2.2.1.2)
  have he : (nativeLengthController p t q h l ∘ incidentHalfLengths q γ) =ᶠ[nhds x]
      incidentNativeController p t q h l γ := by
    filter_upwards [heα, heβ, heδ] with z hα hβ hδ
    exact nativeLengthController_splitHalfLengths (x := ![z 0, z 1, γ])
      (ne_of_gt hq0) hα hβ ha.2.2.1 hδ
  have hs := fderiv_incidentNativeController_surjective hp hp1 ht htq hl hl1
    hh hhq hq hT ha hzero
  rw [← he.fderiv_eq, fderiv_comp x hd hg] at hs
  intro y
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hs y
  exact ⟨fderiv ℝ (incidentHalfLengths q γ) x v, hv⟩

blocks.tex:
(1) Each of the eight arcsine arguments of $N$ is a positive multiple of a
  positive coordinate and is $<1$ by the corresponding strict wall, so
  $\arcsin$ is differentiable there; exponentials and sums are smooth.

  (2) $\ell_\gamma(x)$ is physical by \cref{lem:nfp_split_lengths}(2)
  (its hypotheses are $0<p<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<l<1$ and strict angles; the high
  wall $(h/q)\sin\delta<1$ is part of strictness).  The angles
  $\alpha,\beta,\delta$ are strictly acute at $x$, hence on a neighbourhood
  of $x$, and $\gamma$ is fixed and acute; there
  $N\circ\ell_\gamma=\mathcal N_\gamma$ by \cref{lem:nfp_split_lengths}(1).
  The chain rule and locality of the derivative give
  $D\mathcal N_\gamma(x)=DN(\ell_\gamma(x))\circ D\ell_\gamma(x)$.  The left
  side is surjective by \cref{lem:nrn_incident_transfer}, and a surjective
  composite has surjective outer factor.  No inverse of the three-to-four
  parameter map is needed.

blocks.title: rank in the nonacute chamber
blocks.body:
Let $0<p<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<l<1$, $0<h<q$, $q\ge1$, $L$ physical, $N(L)=0$
  and
  \[
    \arcsin(qL_1)+\arcsin(qL_2)\ge\pi/2 .
  \]
  Then $DN(L)$ is surjective.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_nonacute_incident
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_nonacute_incident
    {p t q h l : ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q)
    (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hphys : NativeLengthPhysical p t q h l L)
    (hzero : nativeLengthController p t q h l L = 0)
    (hT : Real.pi / 2 ≤ Real.arcsin (q * L 1) + Real.arcsin (q * L 2)) :
    Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeLengthController p t q h l) L) := by
  let α := Real.arcsin (L 0)
  let β := Real.arcsin (L 3)
  let γ := Real.arcsin (q * L 1)
  let δ := Real.arcsin (q * L 2)
  let x : Fin 3 → ℝ := ![α + β, α, γ + δ]
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  have hacute {z : ℝ} (hz : 0 < z) (hz1 : z < 1) :
      Real.arcsin z ∈ Ioo 0 (Real.pi / 2) :=
    ⟨Real.arcsin_pos.mpr hz, Real.arcsin_lt_pi_div_two.mpr hz1⟩
  rcases hphys with ⟨hpos, h0, hp0, ht1, hq1, hq2, hh2, hl3, h3⟩
  have ha : StrictAngles q h (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) γ (x 2 - γ) := by
    dsimp [x]
    simp only [add_sub_cancel_left]
    refine ⟨hacute (hpos 0) h0, hacute (hpos 3) h3,
      hacute (mul_pos hq0 (hpos 1)) hq1, hacute (mul_pos hq0 (hpos 2)) hq2, ?_⟩
    dsimp [δ]
    rw [Real.sin_arcsin (by nlinarith [hpos 2]) hq2.le]
    convert hh2 using 1
    field_simp
  have hL : incidentHalfLengths q γ x = L := by
    have hs {z : ℝ} (hz : 0 < z) (hz1 : z < 1) :
        Real.sin (Real.arcsin z) = z := Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith) hz1.le
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> dsimp [incidentHalfLengths, splitHalfLengths, x]
    · exact hs (hpos 0) h0
    · dsimp [γ]
      rw [hs (mul_pos hq0 (hpos 1)) hq1, mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ (ne_of_gt hq0)]
    · rw [add_sub_cancel_left]
      dsimp [δ]
      rw [hs (mul_pos hq0 (hpos 2)) hq2, mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ (ne_of_gt hq0)]
    · rw [add_sub_cancel_left]
      exact hs (hpos 3) h3
  have hz : incidentNativeController p t q h l γ x = 0 := by
    have he := nativeLengthController_splitHalfLengths (p := p) (t := t) (h := h) (l := l)
      (x := ![x 0, x 1, γ])
      (ne_of_gt hq0) ha.1 ha.2.1 ha.2.2.1 ha.2.2.2.1
    change nativeLengthController p t q h l (incidentHalfLengths q γ x) =
      incidentNativeController p t q h l γ x at he
    rw [← he, hL, hzero]
  rw [← hL]
  exact fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_incident_angles
    hp hp1 ht htq hl hl1 hh hhq hq hT ha hz

blocks.tex:
Put $\alpha=\arcsin L_0$, $\beta=\arcsin L_3$, $\gamma=\arcsin(qL_1)$,
  $\delta=\arcsin(qL_2)$ and $x=(\alpha+\beta,\alpha,\gamma+\delta)$.  The
  four pure walls and positivity make the angles acute, and
  $(h/q)\sin\delta=hL_2<1$ is the high wall, so the angles are strict.
  Since $\sin\arcsin=\mathrm{id}$ on $(0,1)$, $\ell_\gamma(x)=L$, and
  $\mathcal N_\gamma(x)=N(L)=0$.  The hypothesis is $T\ge\pi/2$.  Apply

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_equal_pure
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_equal_pure
    {p t h l : ℝ} {L : Fin 4 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (ht : 0 < t) (ht1 : t < 1)
    (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1) (hh : 0 < h) (hh1 : h < 1)
    (hphys : NativeLengthPhysical p t 1 h l L)
    (hzero : nativeLengthController p t 1 h l L = 0) :
    Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeLengthController p t 1 h l) L) := by
  obtain ⟨T, x, ha, hL⟩ := exists_splitHalfLengths_of_physical zero_lt_one hphys
  have hz : nativeSplitController p t 1 h l T x = 0 := by
    rw [← nativeLengthController_splitHalfLengths one_ne_zero
      ha.1 ha.2.1 ha.2.2.1 ha.2.2.2.1, hL, hzero]
  have hroots := (native_zero_iff_of_strictAngles (l := l) hp.le ht.le zero_lt_one ha).mp
    ⟨congrArg Prod.fst hz, congrArg Prod.snd hz⟩
  have hsum := angle_sums_gt_pi_of_seamLow_zero hp hp1 ht ht1 zero_lt_one
    ha.1 ha.2.2.1 hroots.2.1
  have heq : Real.sin (x 0) = Real.sin T := by
    simpa [chord] using sub_eq_zero.mp hroots.1
  have hT : Real.pi / 2 ≤ T := by
    by_contra hn
    have hs := Real.sin_lt_sin_of_lt_of_le_pi_div_two
      (show -(Real.pi / 2) ≤ Real.pi - x 0 by linarith [ha.1.2, ha.2.1.2, Real.pi_pos])
      (le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge hn)) (show Real.pi - x 0 < T by linarith)
    rw [Real.sin_pi_sub, heq] at hs
    exact (lt_irrefl _ hs)
  have hi : incidentNativeController p t 1 h l (x 2) ![x 0, x 1, T] = 0 := hz
  have hia : StrictAngles 1 h (![x 0, x 1, T] 1)
      (![x 0, x 1, T] 0 - ![x 0, x 1, T] 1) (x 2)
      (![x 0, x 1, T] 2 - x 2) := ha
  have hr := fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_incident_angles
    hp hp1 ht ht1 hl hl1 hh hh1 le_rfl hT hia hi
  have hLi : incidentHalfLengths 1 (x 2) ![x 0, x 1, T] = L := hL
  rwa [hLi] at hr

blocks.tex:
By \cref{lem:nfp_split_lengths}(3) with $q=1$, $L=\operatorname{split}(x)$
  for strict angles, and by \cref{lem:nfp_split_lengths}(1) and
  \cref{lem:nfp_native_equations} the chord and both seams vanish.  With
  $q=1$ the chord reads $\sin S=\sin T$, and
  \cref{lem:nrn_incident_obtuse} gives $S+T>\pi$ with $S,T\in(0,\pi)$.

  \emph{$T\ge\pi/2$.}  Suppose $T<\pi/2$.  Then
  $-\pi/2\le\pi-S<T<\pi/2$ (the middle inequality is $S+T>\pi$), and
  strict monotonicity of the sine there gives
  $\sin S=\sin(\pi-S)<\sin T$, contradicting $\sin S=\sin T$.  (In fact
  $T>\pi/2$: $T=\pi/2$ would force $\sin S=1$, $S=\pi/2$ and $S+T=\pi$.
  By symmetry of the argument also $S>\pi/2$, so both pure turns are
  obtuse.)

  Hence $x$ lies in the nonacute chamber and
  \cref{lem:nrn_lengths_transfer}(2), with $q=1\ge1$ and $0<t,h<1=q$,
  gives surjectivity at $\ell_\gamma(x)=L$.  This is the rank statement for
  every physical native zero in the equal-pure chamber, in particular for
  the zero of \cref{thm:nrn_repeated_zero}.

orthogonal core with $0<u,v<1$, as produced by \cref{thm:nrn_negative_zero}.
We treat the chamber $T=\gamma+\delta<\pi/2$.  The argument is by

blocks.body:
Fix $T$ and use the coordinates $x=(S,\alpha,\gamma)$ of
  \cref{def:nfp_split_model} ($\beta=S-\alpha$, $\delta=T-\gamma$).  Let
  $0<p<1$, $0<l<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<h<q$ and strict angles.  Then the
  seam/chord map $\Sigma^T$ has derivative
  \[
    \begin{pmatrix}R&0&0\\ 1&-A&-C\\ 1-B&B&D\end{pmatrix},\qquad
    \det=R\,(BC-AD),
  \]
  i.e.\ \verb|splitDifferential R A B C G| with the excess coefficient
  $G=\operatorname{slope}(h/q,\delta)-1=-D<0$.  If $q>1$, the point is a
  native zero and $AD\ne BC$, then $DN(\operatorname{split}(x))$ is
  surjective.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.hasFDerivAt_splitController_incident
lean.code:
theorem hasFDerivAt_splitController_incident
    {p t q h l T : ℝ} {x : Fin 3 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hq : 0 < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) (x 2) (T - x 2)) :
    HasFDerivAt (splitController p t q h l T)
      (splitDifferential (Real.cos (x 0))
        (1 - angleSlope p (x 1)) (1 - angleSlope l (x 0 - x 1))
        (1 - angleSlope (t / q) (x 2)) (angleSlope (h / q) (T - x 2) - 1)) x := by
  have h0 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 0 x
  have h1 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 1 x
  have h2 := hasFDerivAt_apply (𝕜 := ℝ) (F' := fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ) 2 x
  have hpD := (hasDerivAt_angleDefect hp hp1 ha.1.1 ha.1.2).comp_hasFDerivAt x h1
  have htD := (hasDerivAt_angleDefect (div_pos ht hq) ((div_lt_one hq).2 htq)
    ha.2.2.1.1 ha.2.2.1.2).comp_hasFDerivAt x h2
  have hlD := (hasDerivAt_angleDefect hl hl1 ha.2.1.1 ha.2.1.2).comp_hasFDerivAt x (h0.sub h1)
  have hhD := (hasDerivAt_angleDefect (div_pos hh hq) ((div_lt_one hq).2 hhq)
    ha.2.2.2.1.1 ha.2.2.2.1.2).comp_hasFDerivAt x (h2.const_sub T)
  have hM := ((Real.hasDerivAt_sin (x 0)).comp_hasFDerivAt x h0).sub_const (Real.sin T / q)
  have hLow := (((h0.add_const T).sub_const Real.pi).sub hpD).sub htD
  have hHigh := (((h0.add_const T).sub_const Real.pi).sub hlD).sub hhD
  unfold splitDifferential
  apply hasFDerivAt_pi.mpr
  intro i
  fin_cases i
  · convert hM using 1 <;> simp [splitController, chord]
  · convert hLow using 1
    · ext y
      simp [splitController, seamLow, lowTurn, angleDefect, Function.comp_def]
      ring
    · simp
  · convert hHigh using 1
    · ext y
      simp [splitController, seamHigh, highTurn, angleDefect, Function.comp_def]
      ring
    · ext v
      simp
      ring

theorem fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_fixedTurn_minor
    {p t q h l T : ℝ} {x : Fin 3 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hq : 1 < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) (x 2) (T - x 2))
    (hzero : nativeSplitController p t q h l T x = 0)
    (hminor : (1 - angleSlope p (x 1)) * (1 - angleSlope (h / q) (T - x 2)) ≠
      (1 - angleSlope l (x 0 - x 1)) * (1 - angleSlope (t / q) (x 2))) :
    Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeLengthController p t q h l)
      (splitHalfLengths q T x)) := by
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  have hd := differentiableAt_nativeLengthController_of_physical hp ht hq0 hh hl
    (nativeLengthPhysical_splitHalfLengths hp hp1 ht htq hl hl1 hq0 ha)
  have hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ (splitHalfLengths q T) x := by
    apply differentiableAt_pi.mpr
    intro i
    fin_cases i <;> dsimp [splitHalfLengths] <;> fun_prop
  have hc0 : ContinuousAt (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ => z 0) x := (continuous_apply 0).continuousAt
  have hc1 : ContinuousAt (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ => z 1) x := (continuous_apply 1).continuousAt
  have hc2 : ContinuousAt (fun z : Fin 3 → ℝ => z 2) x := (continuous_apply 2).continuousAt
  have heα := hc1.eventually (Ioo_mem_nhds ha.1.1 ha.1.2)
  have heβ := (hc0.sub hc1).eventually (Ioo_mem_nhds ha.2.1.1 ha.2.1.2)
  have heγ := hc2.eventually (Ioo_mem_nhds ha.2.2.1.1 ha.2.2.1.2)
  have heδ := (hc2.const_sub T).eventually (Ioo_mem_nhds ha.2.2.2.1.1 ha.2.2.2.1.2)
  apply native_rank_of_parametric_rank (f := splitHalfLengths q T)
    (g := nativeSplitController p t q h l T) (x := x) hd hf
  · filter_upwards [heα, heβ, heγ, heδ] with z hα hβ hγ hδ
    exact nativeLengthController_splitHalfLengths (ne_of_gt hq0) hα hβ hγ hδ
  · exact fderiv_nativeSplitController_surjective_of_incident_minor hp hp1 hl hl1
      ht htq hq hh hhq ha hzero hminor

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.splitDifferential_surjective_of_det_ne_zero
lean.code:
theorem splitDifferential_surjective_of_det_ne_zero {R A B C G : ℝ}
    (hR : R ≠ 0) (hD : A * G + B * C ≠ 0) :
    Function.Surjective (splitDifferential R A B C G) := by
  intro y
  let u := y 0 / R
  let v := y 1 - u
  let w := y 2 - (1 - B) * u
  refine ⟨![u, (C * w - G * v) / (A * G + B * C),
    (-A * w - B * v) / (A * G + B * C)], ?_⟩
  rw [splitDifferential_apply]
  have hD' : A * G + C * B ≠ 0 := by simpa only [mul_comm C B] using hD
  have hD'' : G * A + B * C ≠ 0 := by simpa only [mul_comm G A] using hD
  ext i
  fin_cases i <;> simp [u, v, w]
  all_goals field_simp [hR, hD, hD', hD'']
  all_goals nlinarith

theorem fderiv_nativeSplitController_surjective_of_incident_minor
    {p t q h l T : ℝ} {x : Fin 3 → ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hq : 1 < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h (x 1) (x 0 - x 1) (x 2) (T - x 2))
    (hzero : nativeSplitController p t q h l T x = 0)
    (hminor : (1 - angleSlope p (x 1)) * (1 - angleSlope (h / q) (T - x 2)) ≠
      (1 - angleSlope l (x 0 - x 1)) * (1 - angleSlope (t / q) (x 2))) :
    Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeSplitController p t q h l T) x) := by
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  have hz := (native_zero_iff_of_strictAngles (l := l) hp.le ht.le hq0 ha).mp
    ⟨congrArg Prod.fst hzero, congrArg Prod.snd hzero⟩
  have hs : splitController p t q h l T x = 0 := by
    ext i
    fin_cases i
    · exact hz.1
    · exact hz.2.1
    · exact hz.2.2
  have hf := hasFDerivAt_splitController_incident hp hp1 hl hl1 ht htq hq0 hh hhq ha
  have hn := hasFDerivAt_nativeSplitController_of_split hf hs
  have hsin : 0 < Real.sin T := Real.sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi
    (by linarith [ha.2.2.1.1, ha.2.2.2.1.1])
    (by linarith [ha.2.2.1.2, ha.2.2.2.1.2])
  have hcos := cos_first_sum_neg_of_root hp hp1 ht htq hq ha hz.2.1 hz.1
  rw [hn.fderiv]
  have htarget := closureTargetLinearMap_surjective
    (β := x 0 - x 1) (ne_of_gt (div_pos hsin hq0))
    (Complex.I * (Real.sin (x 0 - x 1) : ℂ) * unitPhase (-(x 0)))
  apply htarget.comp
  apply splitDifferential_surjective_of_det_ne_zero
  · simpa using ne_of_lt hcos
  · intro he
    apply hminor
    nlinarith

The rows are computed as in \cref{lem:nfp_split_rank}; the only change is
  that the fourth endpoint is now \emph{below} its pure reading, so the
  $\delta$-term of $K$ is a deficit $\operatorname{def}(h/q,T-\gamma)$
  whose $\gamma$-derivative is $+D$ (instead of an excess with coefficient
  $-G$, $G>0$).  Expanding along the first row,
  $\det=R\bigl((-A)D-(-C)B\bigr)=R(BC-AD)$.  The explicit inverse of
  \cref{lem:nfp_split_rank} works whenever $R\ne0$ and $AG+BC\ne0$, i.e.\
  $BC-AD\ne0$ (\verb|splitDifferential_surjective_of_det_ne_zero|).

  At a native zero, \cref{lem:nfp_native_equations} gives $M=H=K=0$, and
  \cref{lem:nfp_obtuse_first} gives $R=\cos S<0$; its hypotheses are
  $0<p<1$, $0<t<q$, $1<q$ and strict angles, with no condition on $h$.  The
  closure transfer in this chart is the general identity
  \verb|hasFDerivAt_nativeSplitController_of_split| (with constant
  $\varrho=\sin T/q>0$), exactly the calculation of
  \cref{lem:nrn_incident_transfer} without the varying-$\varrho$ term.  The
  passage to four half-lengths is the chain-rule argument of
  \cref{lem:nrn_lengths_transfer} with the map $\operatorname{split}$.

blocks.body:
Let $0<p<1$, $0<l<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<h<q$, $q>1$ and strict angles
  $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$ with $(E,\text{turn defect})=0$.  If $DN$ is
  not surjective at $(\sin\alpha,\sin\gamma/q,\sin\delta/q,\sin\beta)$, then
  \[
    AD=BC\qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \cos(\alpha+\beta)\,(A+B-AD)+\frac{\cos(\gamma+\delta)}q\,(A+B-AB)=0 .

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.incident_minors_vanish_of_not_surjective
lean.code:
theorem incident_minors_vanish_of_not_surjective
    {p t q h l α β γ δ : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hq : 1 < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h α β γ δ)
    (hzero : (nativeHalfClosure p t q h l α β γ δ,
      turnDefect p t q h l α β γ δ) = 0)
    (hnon : ¬Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeLengthController p t q h l)
      ![Real.sin α, Real.sin γ / q, Real.sin δ / q, Real.sin β])) :
    let A := 1 - angleSlope p α
    let B := 1 - angleSlope l β
    let C := 1 - angleSlope (t / q) γ
    let D := 1 - angleSlope (h / q) δ
    A * D = B * C ∧

theorem coreHalfLengths_normalized_cos {u q v : ℝ}
    (hu : 0 < u) (hu1 : u < 1) (hq : 1 < q)
    (hv : 0 < v) (hv1 : v < 1) :
    let L := orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v
    let α := Real.arcsin (L 0)
    let β := Real.arcsin (L 3)
    let γ := Real.arcsin (q * L 1)
    let δ := Real.arcsin (q * L 2)
    let P := Real.tan α / Real.tan γ
    let Q := 1 / (Real.tan γ * Real.tan δ)
    Real.cos (α + β) = (Q - P ^ 2) / Q * Real.cos α * Real.cos β ∧
    Real.cos (γ + δ) / q = P * (Q - 1) / Q * Real.cos α * Real.cos β := by
  have hp := coreHalfLengths_pos hu hu1 hq hv hv1
  obtain ⟨h0, h3, h1, h2⟩ := coreHalfLengths_angle_data hu hu1 hq hv hv1
  obtain ⟨t0, t3, t1, t2⟩ := coreHalfLengths_tan hu hu1 hq hv hv1
  dsimp only
  rw [t0, t1, t2, Real.cos_add, Real.cos_add, h0.2, h3.2, h1.2, h2.2,
    Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith [h0.1.1]) h0.1.2.le,
    Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith [h3.1.1]) h3.1.2.le,
    Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith [h1.1.1]) h1.1.2.le,
    Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith [h2.1.1]) h2.1.2.le]
  constructor <;> field_simp [ne_of_gt hu, ne_of_gt hv, ne_of_gt (show 0 < q by linarith),
    ne_of_gt (hp 0), ne_of_gt (hp 1), ne_of_gt (hp 2), ne_of_gt (hp 3)]

blocks.tex:
Write $d^2=q^2-u^2v^2$ and use the half-sides of
  \cref{lem:nfp_ordered_core}:
  $L_0^2=(q^2-v^2)/d^2$, $L_1^2=(1-v^2)/d^2$, $L_2^2=(1-u^2)/d^2$,
  $L_3^2=(q^2-u^2)/d^2$.  Then for example
  $L_0^2+v^2L_2^2=(q^2-v^2+v^2-u^2v^2)/d^2=1$; the other three identities
  are the same computation.  These are the complementary-square
  identities of the orthogonal quadrilateral, with actual edge indices.

  (2) Each identity has the form $x^2+y^2=1$ with $x,y>0$, so $x\in(0,1)$,
  $\arcsin x\in(0,\pi/2)$ and $\cos\arcsin x=\sqrt{1-x^2}=y$ (positive
  branch).  (3) is $\sin/\cos$.

  (4) $\tan\alpha\tan\delta=\frac{L_0}{vL_2}\cdot\frac{qL_2}{uL_0}=\frac q{uv}$
  and $\tan\beta\tan\gamma=\frac{L_3}{uL_1}\cdot\frac{qL_1}{vL_3}=\frac q{uv}$;
  $uv<1<q$.

  (5) $\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\cos\alpha\cos\beta(1-\tan\alpha\tan\beta)$.  By
  (4) $\tan\beta=\tan\alpha\tan\delta/\tan\gamma$, so
  $\tan\alpha\tan\beta=(\tan\alpha/\tan\gamma)^2\tan\gamma\tan\delta=P^2/Q$.
  For the second, $\cos(\gamma+\delta)=\cos\gamma\cos\delta(1-1/Q)$ and by
  (2)--(3)
  \[
    \frac{\cos\gamma\cos\delta}q=\frac{uv\,L_0L_3}q
    =\frac{L_0}{vL_2}\cdot\frac{vL_3}{qL_1}\cdot(vL_2)(uL_1)
    =P\cos\alpha\cos\beta .
  \]
  These are the normalized cosine identities used below; they are exact
  and carry the positive cosine branches.

blocks.title: Projective coordinates and the rank-loss packet

blocks.label: lem:nrn_projective_coords
blocks.title: projective tangent coordinates
blocks.body:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in(0,\pi/2)$ with
      $\gamma+\delta<\pi/2$, $\tan\alpha\tan\delta=\tan\beta\tan\gamma$ and
      $\tan\alpha\tan\delta>1$.  Put
      \[
        P=\frac{\tan\alpha}{\tan\gamma},\qquad
        Q=\frac1{\tan\gamma\tan\delta},\qquad b=\frac1{\tan\delta}.
      \]
      Then $b>0$, $1<Q<P$ and
      \[
        (\tan\alpha,\tan\beta,\tan\gamma,\tan\delta)
        =\Bigl(\frac{Pb}Q,\ \frac Pb,\ \frac bQ,\ \frac1b\Bigr).
      \]
    \item Let $A,B,C,D\in(0,1)$ with $AD=BC$, and put $r=A/2$, $k=C/2$,
      $\tau=A/B$.  Then $0<r,k<\tfrac12$, $2r<\tau$, $2k<\tau$,
      $B=2r/\tau$ and $D=2k/\tau$.
  \end{enumerate}

theorem incident_projective_parameters {A B C D : ℝ}
    (hA : A ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hB : B ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (hC : C ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hD : D ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (hcross : A * D = B * C) :
    0 < A / 2 ∧ A / 2 < 1 / 2 ∧ 0 < C / 2 ∧ C / 2 < 1 / 2 ∧
    2 * (A / 2) < A / B ∧ 2 * (C / 2) < A / B ∧
    B = 2 * (A / 2) / (A / B) ∧ D = 2 * (C / 2) / (A / B) := by
  refine ⟨half_pos hA.1, by linarith [hA.2], half_pos hC.1, by linarith [hC.2], ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · apply (lt_div_iff₀ hB.1).mpr
    nlinarith [mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hB.2 hA.1]
  · apply (lt_div_iff₀ hB.1).mpr
    nlinarith [mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hD.2 hA.1]
  · field_simp [ne_of_gt hA.1, ne_of_gt hB.1]
  · field_simp [ne_of_gt hA.1, ne_of_gt hB.1]
    nlinarith [hcross]
