lean.code:
theorem acute_projective_coordinates {α β γ δ : ℝ}
    (hα : α ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) (Real.pi / 2))
    (hβ : β ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) (Real.pi / 2))
    (hγ : γ ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) (Real.pi / 2))
    (hδ : δ ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) (Real.pi / 2))
    (hT : γ + δ < Real.pi / 2)
    (hprod : Real.tan α * Real.tan δ = Real.tan β * Real.tan γ)
    (hprod1 : 1 < Real.tan α * Real.tan δ) :
    let P := Real.tan α / Real.tan γ
    let Q := 1 / (Real.tan γ * Real.tan δ)
    let b := 1 / Real.tan δ
    0 < b ∧ 1 < Q ∧ Q < P ∧
      Real.tan α = P * b / Q ∧ Real.tan β = P / b ∧
      Real.tan γ = b / Q ∧ Real.tan δ = 1 / b := by
  have ha := Real.tan_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi_div_two hα.1 hα.2
  have hb := Real.tan_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi_div_two hβ.1 hβ.2
  have hc := Real.tan_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi_div_two hγ.1 hγ.2
  have hd := Real.tan_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi_div_two hδ.1 hδ.2
  have hcg : 0 < Real.cos γ := Real.cos_pos_of_mem_Ioo
    ⟨by linarith [Real.pi_pos, hγ.1], hγ.2⟩
  have hcd : 0 < Real.cos δ := Real.cos_pos_of_mem_Ioo
    ⟨by linarith [Real.pi_pos, hδ.1], hδ.2⟩
  have hct : 0 < Real.cos (γ + δ) := Real.cos_pos_of_mem_Ioo
    ⟨by linarith [Real.pi_pos, hγ.1, hδ.1], hT⟩
  have htprod : Real.tan γ * Real.tan δ < 1 := by
    rw [Real.cos_add] at hct
    rw [Real.tan_eq_sin_div_cos, Real.tan_eq_sin_div_cos]
    rw [div_mul_div_comm, div_lt_one (mul_pos hcg hcd)]
    linarith
  dsimp only
  refine ⟨one_div_pos.mpr hd, (one_lt_div (mul_pos hc hd)).mpr htprod, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · apply (div_lt_div_iff₀ (mul_pos hc hd) hc).mpr
    nlinarith [mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hprod1 hc]
  · field_simp
  · apply (mul_right_cancel₀ (ne_of_gt hc))
    field_simp
    nlinarith [hprod]
  · field_simp
  · field_simp

blocks.tex:
(1) $\cos(\gamma+\delta)>0$ gives
  $\cos\gamma\cos\delta>\sin\gamma\sin\delta$, i.e.\
  $\tan\gamma\tan\delta<1$ and $Q>1$.  $P/Q=\tan\alpha\tan\delta>1$ gives
  $P>Q$.  The four formulas: $\tan\delta=1/b$;
  $\tan\gamma=1/(Q\tan\delta)=b/Q$; $\tan\alpha=P\tan\gamma=Pb/Q$; and
  $\tan\beta=\tan\alpha\tan\delta/\tan\gamma=(Pb/Q)(1/b)(Q/b)=P/b$.

  (2) $B=A/\tau$ by definition; $D=BC/A=C/\tau$ by $AD=BC$.  Then
  $2r<\tau$ is $A<A/B$, i.e.\ $B<1$, and $2k<\tau$ is $C<A/B$, i.e.\
  $BC<A$, i.e.\ $AD<A$, i.e.\ $D<1$.

Notation: the \emph{projective} letters $P,Q,r,k,\tau$ and
$\mathcal B=b^2$ are not the curvature readings $p,q$, the defect slope $B$
or the angular turn $T$.  In Lean the fields of the packet below are named
\verb|P|, \verb|Q|, \verb|B|, \verb|r|, \verb|k|, \verb|T|; its \verb|B| is
$\mathcal B$ and its \verb|T| is $\tau$.  In
\verb|NativeIncidentProjective| the same quantities appear as lower-case
\verb|p q B r k T|.

blocks.label: lem:nrn_tangent_turns
blocks.title: tangent form of the two seams
blocks.body:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For $z\in(0,\pi/2)$,
      $\tan\operatorname{atom}(a,z)=\operatorname{slope}(a,z)\tan z$.
    \item If $\cos x,\cos y,\cos z,\cos w\ne0$ and $x+y+z+w=\pi$, then
      \[
        (\tan z\tan w-1)(\tan x+\tan y)=(\tan z+\tan w)(1-\tan x\tan y).
      \]
    \item In the coordinates of \cref{lem:nrn_projective_coords}, the low
      seam $\operatorname{atom}(p,\alpha)+\operatorname{atom}(t/q,\gamma)
      +\beta+\delta=\pi$ implies
      \[
        \mathrm{(T1)}\quad
        Q(P-\mathcal B)\bigl(P(1-2r)+(1-2k)\bigr)
        -(P+1)\bigl(Q^2-P\mathcal B(1-2r)(1-2k)\bigr)=0,
      \]
      and the high seam
      $\operatorname{atom}(h/q,\delta)+\operatorname{atom}(l,\beta)
      +\alpha+\gamma=\pi$ implies
      \[
        \mathrm{(T2)}\quad
        (P\mathcal B-Q^2)\,\tau\,\bigl(\tau-2k+P(\tau-2r)\bigr)
        -Q(P+1)\bigl(\mathcal B\tau^2-P(\tau-2k)(\tau-2r)\bigr)=0 .
      \]
  \end{enumerate}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.tangent_turn_polynomial
lean.code:
theorem tangent_turn_polynomial {x y z w : ℝ}
    (hx : Real.cos x ≠ 0) (hy : Real.cos y ≠ 0)
    (hz : Real.cos z ≠ 0) (hw : Real.cos w ≠ 0)
    (hsum : x + y + z + w = Real.pi) :
    (Real.tan z * Real.tan w - 1) * (Real.tan x + Real.tan y) =
      (Real.tan z + Real.tan w) * (1 - Real.tan x * Real.tan y) := by
  have hs : Real.sin (x + y + z + w) = 0 := by rw [hsum, Real.sin_pi]
  simp only [Real.sin_add, Real.cos_add] at hs
  simp only [Real.tan_eq_sin_div_cos]
  field_simp [hx, hy, hz, hw]
  nlinarith [hs]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.second_projective_turn_polynomial
lean.code:
theorem second_projective_turn_polynomial {P Q b r k T : ℝ}
    (hQ : Q ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hT : T ≠ 0)
    (hturn : ((P * b / Q) * (b / Q) - 1) *
        ((1 / b) * (1 - 2 * k / T) + (P / b) * (1 - 2 * r / T)) =
      (P * b / Q + b / Q) *
        (1 - ((1 / b) * (1 - 2 * k / T)) * ((P / b) * (1 - 2 * r / T)))) :
    (P * b ^ 2 - Q ^ 2) * T * (T - 2 * k + P * (T - 2 * r)) -
      Q * (P + 1) * (b ^ 2 * T ^ 2 - P * (T - 2 * k) * (T - 2 * r)) = 0 := by
  field_simp [hQ, hb, hT] at hturn
  nlinarith [hturn]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.first_projective_turn_polynomial
lean.code:
theorem first_projective_turn_polynomial {P Q b r k : ℝ}
    (hQ : Q ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0)
    (hturn : ((P / b) * (1 / b) - 1) *
        ((P * b / Q) * (1 - 2 * r) + (b / Q) * (1 - 2 * k)) =
      (P / b + 1 / b) *
        (1 - ((P * b / Q) * (1 - 2 * r)) * ((b / Q) * (1 - 2 * k)))) :
    Q * (P - b ^ 2) * (P * (1 - 2 * r) + (1 - 2 * k)) -
      (P + 1) * (Q ^ 2 - P * b ^ 2 * (1 - 2 * r) * (1 - 2 * k)) = 0 := by
  field_simp [hQ, hb] at hturn
  nlinarith [hturn]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.tan_angleAtom_eq_slope_mul_tan
lean.code:
theorem tan_angleAtom_eq_slope_mul_tan {a z : ℝ}
    (hz : z ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) (Real.pi / 2)) :
    Real.tan (angleAtom a z) = angleSlope a z * Real.tan z := by
  have hc : Real.cos z ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt
    (Real.cos_pos_of_mem_Ioo ⟨by linarith [Real.pi_pos, hz.1], hz.2⟩)
  rw [angleAtom, Real.tan_arcsin, angleSlope, Real.tan_eq_sin_div_cos]
  field_simp [hc]

blocks.tex:
(1) $\tan\arcsin y=y/\sqrt{1-y^2}$ with $y=a\sin z$, and
  $\operatorname{slope}(a,z)\tan z=\frac{a\cos z}{\sqrt{1-a^2\sin^2z}}
  \cdot\frac{\sin z}{\cos z}$.

  (2) $0=\sin\bigl((x+y)+(z+w)\bigr)
  =\sin(x+y)\cos(z+w)+\cos(x+y)\sin(z+w)$; expand all four and divide by
  $\cos x\cos y\cos z\cos w\ne0$:
  $(\tan x+\tan y)(1-\tan z\tan w)+(1-\tan x\tan y)(\tan z+\tan w)=0$.
  Only the four \emph{individual} cosines are divided out, so the identity
  remains valid if an intermediate sum such as $x+y$ is a right angle.

  (3) The slopes are $1-A=1-2r$, $1-C=1-2k$, $1-D=1-2k/\tau$,
  $1-B=1-2r/\tau$ (\cref{lem:nrn_projective_coords}(2)).  For the low seam
  take $x=\operatorname{atom}(p,\alpha)$, $y=\operatorname{atom}(t/q,\gamma)$,
  $z=\beta$, $w=\delta$: by (1),
  $\tan x=\frac{Pb}Q(1-2r)$, $\tan y=\frac bQ(1-2k)$, $\tan z=\frac Pb$,
  $\tan w=\frac1b$.  The endpoint atoms are acute
  ($0<\operatorname{atom}(a,z)<z<\pi/2$ for $0<a<1$), so their cosines are
  positive.  Substituting into (2),
  \[
    \Bigl(\frac P{b^2}-1\Bigr)\frac bQ\bigl(P(1-2r)+(1-2k)\bigr)
    =\frac{P+1}b\Bigl(1-\frac{Pb^2}{Q^2}(1-2r)(1-2k)\Bigr),
  \]
  and multiplying by $bQ^2$ gives (T1).  For the high seam take
  $x=\operatorname{atom}(h/q,\delta)$, $y=\operatorname{atom}(l,\beta)$,
  $z=\alpha$, $w=\gamma$ with $\tan x=\frac1b(1-\frac{2k}\tau)$,
  $\tan y=\frac Pb(1-\frac{2r}\tau)$, $\tan z=\frac{Pb}Q$,
  $\tan w=\frac bQ$; clearing the nonzero denominators $b,Q,\tau$ gives
  (T2).

blocks.label: lem:nrn_affine
blocks.title: the affine relation from the second minor
blocks.body:
Let $\lambda\ne0$, $B\ne0$, $R=\lambda(Q-P^2)$, $W=\lambda P(Q-1)$,
  $AD=BC$ and $R(A+B-AD)+W(A+B-AB)=0$.  Then, with $\tau=A/B$, $r=A/2$,
  $k=C/2$,
  \[
    \mathrm{(Aff)}\quad
    -(P+1)(P-Q)(1+\tau)+2(P^2-Q)k-2P(Q-1)r=0 .
  \]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.projective_affine_of_incident_minor
lean.code:
theorem projective_affine_of_incident_minor
    {P Q K A B C D R W : ℝ} (hK : K ≠ 0) (_hA : A ≠ 0) (hB : B ≠ 0)
    (hR : R = K * (Q - P ^ 2)) (hW : W = K * P * (Q - 1))
    (hcross : A * D = B * C)
    (hminor : R * (A + B - A * D) + W * (A + B - A * B) = 0) :
    -(P + 1) * (P - Q) * (1 + A / B) +
      2 * (P ^ 2 - Q) * (C / 2) - 2 * P * (Q - 1) * (A / 2) = 0 := by
  rw [hR, hW] at hminor
  have hm : (Q - P ^ 2) * (A + B - A * D) +
      P * (Q - 1) * (A + B - A * B) = 0 := by
    apply (mul_left_cancel₀ hK)
    nlinarith [hminor]
  field_simp [hB]
  rw [hcross] at hm
  linear_combination hm

blocks.tex:
Divide the minor by $\lambda$ and replace $AD$ by $BC$:
  $(Q-P^2)(A+B-BC)+P(Q-1)(A+B-AB)=0$.  Divide by $B$:
  \[
    (Q-P^2)(\tau+1-C)+P(Q-1)(\tau+1-A)=0 .
  \]
  Since $Q-P^2+P(Q-1)=(P+1)(Q-P)$, this is
  $(P+1)(Q-P)(1+\tau)-(Q-P^2)2k-P(Q-1)2r=0$, which is (Aff).

blocks.label: def:nrn_rank_loss_packet
blocks.title: the rank-loss packet
blocks.body:
An \emph{incident projective rank-loss packet} consists of reals
  $P,Q,\mathcal B,r,k,\tau$ with
  \[
    1<Q<P,\quad \mathcal B>0,\quad 0<r<\tfrac12,\quad 0<k<\tfrac12,\quad
    2r<\tau,\quad 2k<\tau,
  \]
  satisfying (Aff), (T1) and (T2).  The left-hand sides of (T1), (T2),
  (Aff) are the polynomials \verb|turnOne|, \verb|turnTwo|,
  \verb|affineRelation|.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.IncidentProjectiveRankLoss
lean.code:
structure IncidentProjectiveRankLoss where
  P : ℝ
  Q : ℝ
  B : ℝ
  r : ℝ
  k : ℝ
  T : ℝ
  one_lt_Q : 1 < Q
  Q_lt_P : Q < P
  B_pos : 0 < B
  r_pos : 0 < r
  r_half : r < 1 / 2
  k_pos : 0 < k
  k_half : k < 1 / 2
  r_T : 2 * r < T
  k_T : 2 * k < T
  affine : -(P + 1) * (P - Q) * (1 + T) +
    2 * (P ^ 2 - Q) * k - 2 * P * (Q - 1) * r = 0
  turnOne : Q * (P - B) * (P * (1 - 2 * r) + (1 - 2 * k)) -
    (P + 1) * (Q ^ 2 - P * B * (1 - 2 * r) * (1 - 2 * k)) = 0
  turnTwo : (P * B - Q ^ 2) * T * (T - 2 * k + P * (T - 2 * r)) -
    Q * (P + 1) * (B * T ^ 2 - P * (T - 2 * k) * (T - 2 * r)) = 0

blocks.label: lem:nrn_rank_loss_packet
blocks.title: native rank loss produces a packet
blocks.body:
Let $0<p<1$, $0<l<1$, $0<t<q$, $0<h<q$, $q>1$ and strict angles
  $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$ with $\gamma+\delta<\pi/2$,
  $\tan\alpha\tan\delta=\tan\beta\tan\gamma>1$, the normalized cosine
  identities of \cref{lem:nrn_core_trig}(5), and $(E,\text{turn
  defect})=0$.  If $DN$ is not surjective at
  $(\sin\alpha,\sin\gamma/q,\sin\delta/q,\sin\beta)$, then a rank-loss
  packet exists.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.incidentProjectiveRankLoss_of_angles
lean.code:
theorem incidentProjectiveRankLoss_of_angles
    {p t q h l α β γ δ : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hq : 1 < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (ha : StrictAngles q h α β γ δ)
    (hT : γ + δ < Real.pi / 2)
    (hprod : Real.tan α * Real.tan δ = Real.tan β * Real.tan γ)
    (hprod1 : 1 < Real.tan α * Real.tan δ)
    (hcos : let P := Real.tan α / Real.tan γ
      let Q := 1 / (Real.tan γ * Real.tan δ)
      Real.cos (α + β) = (Q - P ^ 2) / Q * Real.cos α * Real.cos β ∧
        Real.cos (γ + δ) / q = P * (Q - 1) / Q * Real.cos α * Real.cos β)
    (hzero : (nativeHalfClosure p t q h l α β γ δ,
      turnDefect p t q h l α β γ δ) = 0)
    (hnon : ¬Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeLengthController p t q h l)
      ![Real.sin α, Real.sin γ / q, Real.sin δ / q, Real.sin β])) :
    Nonempty IncidentProjectiveRankLoss := by
  let P := Real.tan α / Real.tan γ
  let Q := 1 / (Real.tan γ * Real.tan δ)
  let b := 1 / Real.tan δ
  let A := 1 - angleSlope p α
  let B := 1 - angleSlope l β
  let C := 1 - angleSlope (t / q) γ
  let D := 1 - angleSlope (h / q) δ
  let r := A / 2
  let k := C / 2
  let T := A / B
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  obtain ⟨hb, hQ, hQP, hαtan, hβtan, hγtan, hδtan⟩ :=
    acute_projective_coordinates ha.1 ha.2.1 ha.2.2.1 ha.2.2.2.1 hT hprod hprod1
  change 0 < b at hb
  change 1 < Q at hQ
  change Q < P at hQP
  change Real.tan α = P * b / Q at hαtan
  change Real.tan β = P / b at hβtan
  change Real.tan γ = b / Q at hγtan
  change Real.tan δ = 1 / b at hδtan
  have hA := defectSlope_mem_Ioo hp hp1 ha.1
  have hB := defectSlope_mem_Ioo hl hl1 ha.2.1
  have hC := defectSlope_mem_Ioo (div_pos ht hq0) ((div_lt_one hq0).mpr htq) ha.2.2.1
  have hD := defectSlope_mem_Ioo (div_pos hh hq0) ((div_lt_one hq0).mpr hhq) ha.2.2.2.1
  obtain ⟨hcross, hminor⟩ := incident_minors_vanish_of_not_surjective
    hp hp1 hl hl1 ht htq hq hh hhq ha hzero hnon
  change A * D = B * C at hcross
  change Real.cos (α + β) * (A + B - A * D) +
    (Real.cos (γ + δ) / q) * (A + B - A * B) = 0 at hminor
  obtain ⟨hr0, hr1, hk0, hk1, hrT, hkT, hBT, hDT⟩ :=
    incident_projective_parameters hA hB hC hD hcross
  change 0 < r at hr0
  change r < 1 / 2 at hr1
  change 0 < k at hk0
  change k < 1 / 2 at hk1
  change 2 * r < T at hrT
  change 2 * k < T at hkT
  change B = 2 * r / T at hBT
  change D = 2 * k / T at hDT
  have hT0 : 0 < T := by linarith
  have hQ0 : 0 < Q := by linarith
  have hcα : 0 < Real.cos α := Real.cos_pos_of_mem_Ioo
    ⟨by linarith [ha.1.1, Real.pi_pos], ha.1.2⟩
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
Define $P,Q,b$ as in \cref{lem:nrn_projective_coords}(1): $b>0$,
  $1<Q<P$ and the tangent formulas hold.  The defect slopes lie in $(0,1)$
  (\cref{lem:nfp_angle_slopes}).  By \cref{lem:nrn_minors_vanish}, $AD=BC$
  and the second minor vanishes; \cref{lem:nrn_projective_coords}(2) gives
  $r,k,\tau$ with $0<r,k<\tfrac12$, $2r<\tau$, $2k<\tau$ (so $\tau>0$),
  $B=2r/\tau$, $D=2k/\tau$.

  Put $\lambda=\cos\alpha\cos\beta/Q>0$.  The normalized cosine identities
  say $R=\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\lambda(Q-P^2)$ and
  $W=\cos(\gamma+\delta)/q=\lambda P(Q-1)$, so \cref{lem:nrn_affine}
  gives (Aff).  By \cref{lem:nfp_native_equations} the native zero has
  $H=K=0$, i.e.\ the two seams $\operatorname{atom}(p,\alpha)+
  \operatorname{atom}(t/q,\gamma)+\beta+\delta=\pi$ and
  $\operatorname{atom}(h/q,\delta)+\operatorname{atom}(l,\beta)+\alpha+
  \gamma=\pi$.  \Cref{lem:nrn_tangent_turns}(3) gives (T1) and (T2) with
  $\mathcal B=b^2>0$.  All strict inequalities of the packet have been
  derived; the packet is \emph{produced} by native rank loss, not assumed.

blocks.label: def:nrn_elimination_polys
blocks.title: elimination polynomials

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeIncidentProjective.polyC
lean.code: def polyC (p q B r : ℝ) : ℝ := B * p * polyD p q r + q * polyA p q r

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeIncidentProjective.projectiveD0
lean.code: def projectiveD0 (p q r : ℝ) : ℝ := p * (p + 1) * r - (p ^ 2 - q)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeIncidentProjective.projectiveH
lean.code: def projectiveH (p q r k : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 * k * projectiveD0 p q r + projectiveN p q r

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeIncidentProjective.projectiveN
lean.code: def projectiveN (p q r : ℝ) : ℝ := (p + 1) * (p - q) + 2 * p * (q - 1) * r

blocks.label: lem:nrn_projective_H
blocks.title: elimination of $\mathcal B$ and $\tau$
blocks.body:
Let $1<Q<P$, $0<r<\tfrac12$, $k>0$, $2r<\tau$ and let (T1), (T2), (Aff)
  hold (for any real $\mathcal B$).  Then $\mathsf H=0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeIncidentProjective.projectiveH_eq_zero
lean.code:
theorem projectiveH_eq_zero {p q B r k T : ℝ}
    (hq : 1 < q) (hqp : q < p) (hr : 0 < r)
    (hk : 0 < k) (hTr : 2 * r < T)
    (hf1 : turnOne p q B r k = 0) (hf2 : turnTwo p q B r k T = 0)
    (haff : affineRelation p q r k T = 0) : projectiveH p q r k = 0 := by
  have hp0 : 0 < p := by linarith
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  have hp1 : 0 < p + 1 := by linarith
  have hpq : 0 < p - q := by linarith
  have hT : T = affineT p q r k := by
    apply (eq_div_iff (mul_ne_zero hp1.ne' hpq.ne')).mpr
    unfold affineRelation at haff
    nlinarith [haff]
  have hres : coeffOne p q r k * constTwo p q r k T -
      constOne p q r k * coeffTwo p q r k T = 0 := by
    unfold turnOne at hf1
    unfold turnTwo at hf2
    unfold coeffOne constOne coeffTwo constTwo
    linear_combination
      (-q * (p * (1 - 2 * r) + (1 - 2 * k)) +
        (p + 1) * p * (1 - 2 * r) * (1 - 2 * k)) * hf2 -
      (p * T * (T - 2 * k + p * (T - 2 * r)) - q * (p + 1) * T ^ 2) * hf1
  have hprod : 8 * p * q * (r - k) *
      (k * (p ^ 2 - q) + p ^ 2 * r * (q - 1)) * projectiveH p q r k = 0 := by
    rw [← elimination_identity hp1.ne' hpq.ne', ← hT, hres, mul_zero]
  have hrk : r - k ≠ 0 := by
    intro heq
    have hkr : k = r := by linarith
    have hid : affineRelation p q r r T = (p + 1) * (p - q) * (2 * r - 1 - T) := by
      unfold affineRelation
      ring
    rw [hkr, hid] at haff
    have ht : 2 * r - 1 - T = 0 :=
      (mul_eq_zero.mp haff).resolve_left (mul_ne_zero hp1.ne' hpq.ne')
    linarith
  have hbranch : 0 < k * (p ^ 2 - q) + p ^ 2 * r * (q - 1) := by
    have hpsq : 0 < p ^ 2 - q := by nlinarith
    exact add_pos (mul_pos hk hpsq) (mul_pos (mul_pos (sq_pos_of_pos hp0) hr) (by linarith))
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hprod).resolve_left
    (mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero (by norm_num) hp0.ne') hq0.ne') hrk)
      hbranch.ne')

blocks.tex:
\emph{Eliminate $\mathcal B$.}  Both turn equations are affine in
  $\mathcal B$: $\mathrm{(T1)}=c_1\mathcal B+e_1$ and
  $\mathrm{(T2)}=c_2\mathcal B+e_2$ with
  \begin{align*}
    c_1&=-Q\bigl(P(1-2r)+(1-2k)\bigr)+(P+1)P(1-2r)(1-2k),\\
    e_1&=QP\bigl(P(1-2r)+(1-2k)\bigr)-(P+1)Q^2,\\
    c_2&=P\tau\bigl(\tau-2k+P(\tau-2r)\bigr)-Q(P+1)\tau^2,\\
    e_2&=-Q^2\tau\bigl(\tau-2k+P(\tau-2r)\bigr)+Q(P+1)P(\tau-2k)(\tau-2r).
  \end{align*}
  The combination $c_1\cdot\mathrm{(T2)}-c_2\cdot\mathrm{(T1)}$ gives
  $c_1e_2-e_1c_2=0$.

  \emph{Eliminate $\tau$.}  $(P+1)(P-Q)>0$, so (Aff) is solved by
  \[
    \tau=\tau^*(r,k)=\frac{2(P^2-Q)k-2P(Q-1)r-(P+1)(P-Q)}{(P+1)(P-Q)} .
  \]
  The exact rational identity (valid whenever $(P+1)(P-Q)\ne0$; proved by
  clearing this denominator and expanding)
  \[
    (P+1)(P-Q)\bigl(c_1e_2-e_1c_2\bigr)\big|_{\tau=\tau^*}
    =8PQ\,(r-k)\,\bigl(k(P^2-Q)+P^2r(Q-1)\bigr)\,\mathsf H
  \]
  shows that the product on the right vanishes.

  \emph{Cancel the spurious factors.}  $8PQ\ne0$.  If $r=k$, then
  $P^2-Q-PQ+P=(P+1)(P-Q)$ turns (Aff) into
  $(P+1)(P-Q)(2r-1-\tau)=0$, so $\tau=2r-1<2r$, contradicting $2r<\tau$.
  Finally $P^2>P>Q$, so $k(P^2-Q)+P^2r(Q-1)>0$.  Hence $\mathsf H=0$.  No
  resultant computed outside Lean and no division by an unsigned factor
  occurs.

blocks.label: lem:nrn_projective_interval
blocks.title: the forced interval
blocks.body:
Let $1<Q<P$ and $\mathsf H=0$.
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item If (Aff) holds, then $(P-Q)\tau=2kPr$.
    \item If (T1) holds, then $\operatorname{polyC}(r)=0$.
    \item If $r>0$, $0<k<\tfrac12$, $2k<\tau$ and $(P-Q)\tau=2kPr$, then
      \[
        \frac{P-Q}P<r<\frac{Q-1}{P+2Q-1}.
      \]
  \end{enumerate}

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeIncidentProjective.projective_polyC_eq_zero
lean.code:
theorem projective_polyC_eq_zero {p q B r k : ℝ} (hp : p + 1 ≠ 0)
    (hf1 : turnOne p q B r k = 0) (hH : projectiveH p q r k = 0) :
    polyC p q B r = 0 := by
  have hid : projectiveD0 p q r * turnOne p q B r k + (p + 1) * polyC p q B r =
      (2 * B * p ^ 2 * r - B * p ^ 2 + 2 * B * p * r - B * p + B * q - p * q) *
        projectiveH p q r k := by
    unfold projectiveH projectiveD0 turnOne polyC polyD polyA projectiveN
    ring
  rw [hf1, hH, mul_zero, mul_zero, zero_add] at hid
  exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hid).resolve_left hp

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeIncidentProjective.projective_T_relation
lean.code:
theorem projective_T_relation {p q r k T : ℝ} (hp : p + 1 ≠ 0)
    (haff : affineRelation p q r k T = 0) (hH : projectiveH p q r k = 0) :
    (p - q) * T = 2 * k * p * r := by
  have hid : (p + 1) * ((p - q) * T - 2 * k * p * r) +
      projectiveH p q r k + affineRelation p q r k T = 0 := by
    unfold projectiveH projectiveD0 projectiveN affineRelation
    ring
  rw [hH, haff, add_zero, add_zero] at hid
  exact sub_eq_zero.mp ((mul_eq_zero.mp hid).resolve_left hp)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeIncidentProjective.projective_forced_interval
lean.code:
theorem projective_forced_interval {p q r k T : ℝ}
    (hq : 1 < q) (hqp : q < p) (hr : 0 < r) (hk : 0 < k) (hkhalf : k < 1 / 2)
    (hTk : 2 * k < T) (hH : projectiveH p q r k = 0)
    (hT : (p - q) * T = 2 * k * p * r) :
    (p - q) / p < r ∧ r < (q - 1) / (p + 2 * q - 1) := by
  have hp : 0 < p := by linarith
  have hpq : 0 < p - q := by linarith
  have hden : 0 < p + 2 * q - 1 := by linarith
  have hN : 0 < projectiveN p q r := by
    unfold projectiveN
    exact add_pos (mul_pos (by linarith) hpq)
      (mul_pos (mul_pos (mul_pos (by norm_num) hp) (by linarith)) hr)
  have hD : projectiveD0 p q r < 0 := by
    unfold projectiveH at hH
    by_contra hn
    have := mul_nonneg (show 0 ≤ 2 * k by linarith) (le_of_not_gt hn)
    linarith
  constructor
  · have hscaled := mul_pos hpq (sub_pos.mpr hTk)
    have hprod : 0 < (2 * k) * (p * r - (p - q)) := by nlinarith [hT]
    have hpr : p - q < p * r := sub_pos.mp (pos_of_mul_pos_right hprod (by linarith))
    exact (div_lt_iff₀ hp).mpr (by nlinarith)
  · have hprod : (1 - 2 * k) * projectiveD0 p q r < 0 :=
      mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg (by linarith) hD
    have hid : projectiveN p q r + projectiveD0 p q r =
        p * (r * (p + 2 * q - 1) - (q - 1)) := by
      unfold projectiveN projectiveD0
      ring
    have hsum : projectiveN p q r + projectiveD0 p q r < 0 := by
      unfold projectiveH at hH
      nlinarith
    rw [hid] at hsum
    have hinner : r * (p + 2 * q - 1) - (q - 1) < 0 :=
      neg_of_mul_neg_right hsum hp.le
    exact (lt_div_iff₀ hden).mpr (by linarith)

blocks.tex:
(1) The polynomial identity
  $(P+1)\bigl((P-Q)\tau-2kPr\bigr)+\mathsf H+\mathrm{(Aff)}=0$ and
  $P+1\ne0$.

  (2) The polynomial identity
  \[
    D_0\cdot\mathrm{(T1)}+(P+1)\operatorname{polyC}(r)
    =\bigl(2\mathcal BP^2r-\mathcal BP^2+2\mathcal BPr-\mathcal BP
      +\mathcal BQ-PQ\bigr)\mathsf H
  \]
  and $P+1\ne0$.

  (3) $\mathsf N>0$ since $P>Q$, $Q>1$, $r>0$.  From
  $\mathsf H=2kD_0+\mathsf N=0$ and $k>0$ we get $D_0<0$ (without dividing
  by $D_0$: if $D_0\ge0$ then $\mathsf H\ge\mathsf N>0$).
  \emph{Lower bound:} multiply $2k<\tau$ by $P-Q>0$:
  $2k(P-Q)<(P-Q)\tau=2kPr$, so $P-Q<Pr$ ($k>0$), i.e.\ $r>(P-Q)/P$.
  \emph{Upper bound:} $\mathsf N+D_0=\mathsf H+(1-2k)D_0=(1-2k)D_0<0$
  since $k<\tfrac12$, and the identity
  $\mathsf N+D_0=P\bigl(r(P+2Q-1)-(Q-1)\bigr)$ gives
  $r(P+2Q-1)<Q-1$; the denominator $P+2Q-1$ is positive.

lean.code:
theorem polyA_neg_and_polyD_neg_of_interval {p q r : ℝ}
    (hq : 1 < q) (hqp : q < p)
    (hlo : (p - q) / p < r) (hhi : r < (q - 1) / (p + 2 * q - 1)) :
    polyA p q r < 0 ∧ polyD p q r < 0 := by
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  have hp : 0 < p := by linarith
  have hp1 : 0 < p + 1 := by linarith
  have hden : 0 < p + 2 * q - 1 := by linarith
  have hgap : 0 < p ^ 2 - 2 * q + 1 := by nlinarith
  have hpq : 0 < p + q := by linarith
  have hcross := (div_lt_div_iff₀ hp hden).mp (hlo.trans hhi)
  have hbound : p ^ 2 - 2 * q ^ 2 + q < 0 := by nlinarith
  have hright : (q - 1) / (p + 2 * q - 1) < (p ^ 2 - q) / (p * (p + 1)) := by
    apply (div_lt_div_iff₀ hden (mul_pos hp hp1)).mpr
    nlinarith [mul_pos hpq hgap]
  have hAleft : polyA p q ((p - q) / p) < 0 := by
    rw [polyA_at_left hp.ne']
    have := mul_pos (mul_pos hp hq0) (sub_pos.mpr hqp)
    nlinarith
  have hAright : polyA p q ((p ^ 2 - q) / (p * (p + 1))) < 0 := by
    rw [polyA_at_outer_right hp.ne' hp1.ne']
    exact div_neg_of_neg_of_pos
      (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos (neg_neg_of_pos hp) hpq) hgap)
      (sq_pos_of_pos hp1)
  have hDleft : polyD p q ((p - q) / p) < 0 := by
    rw [polyD_at_left hp.ne']
    have hinner : p ^ 2 - p * q - 2 * q ^ 2 + q < 0 := by
      nlinarith [mul_pos hp hq0]
    exact div_neg_of_neg_of_pos (mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg (sub_pos.mpr hqp) hinner) hp
  have hDright : polyD p q ((q - 1) / (p + 2 * q - 1)) < 0 := by
    rw [polyD_at_right hden.ne']
    exact div_neg_of_neg_of_pos
      (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos (neg_neg_of_pos hq0) hpq) hgap)
      (sq_pos_of_pos hden)
  constructor
  · exact quadratic_neg_between (by positivity : 0 ≤ 2 * p ^ 3)
      hlo (hhi.trans hright) hAleft hAright
  · have hcoeff : 0 ≤ 2 * p ^ 2 + 2 * p * q - 2 * p := by
      have := mul_pos (mul_pos (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 2) hp)
        (show 0 < p + q - 1 by linarith)
      nlinarith
    exact quadratic_neg_between hcoeff hlo hhi hDleft hDright

blocks.tex:
\emph{Chord inequality.}  For a quadratic $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$ and any
  $x_0<x<x_1$,
  \[
    (x_1-x_0)f(x)=(x_1-x)f(x_0)+(x-x_0)f(x_1)-a(x-x_0)(x_1-x)(x_1-x_0).
  \]
  If $a\ge0$ and $f(x_0),f(x_1)<0$, the right side is negative, so
  $f(x)<0$.

  \emph{Consequences of the interval.}  $P^2-2Q+1>Q^2-2Q+1\ge0$.  The
  interval is nonempty, and cross-multiplying $r_-<r_+$ (positive
  denominators) gives $(P-Q)(P+2Q-1)<P(Q-1)$, i.e.\
  \[
    P^2-2Q^2+Q<0 .
  \]
  Put $r_A=\frac{P^2-Q}{P(P+1)}$.  Then $r_+<r_A$, because
  $(P^2-Q)(P+2Q-1)-(Q-1)P(P+1)=(P+Q)(P^2-2Q+1)>0$.

  \emph{Endpoint values} (rational identities):
  \begin{align*}
    \operatorname{polyA}(r_-)&=-PQ(P-Q)<0,\\
    \operatorname{polyA}(r_A)&=-\frac{P(P+Q)(P^2-2Q+1)}{(P+1)^2}<0,\\
    \operatorname{polyD}(r_-)&=\frac{(P-Q)(P^2-PQ-2Q^2+Q)}P<0,\\
    \operatorname{polyD}(r_+)&=-\frac{Q(P+Q)(P^2-2Q+1)}{(P+2Q-1)^2}<0 .
  \end{align*}
  For the third, $P^2-PQ-2Q^2+Q=(P^2-2Q^2+Q)-PQ<0$ uses the interval
  consequence above.

  \emph{Conclusion.}  polyA has leading coefficient $2P^3>0$ and is
  negative at $r_-$ and at $r_A>r_+>r$; by the chord inequality on
  $[r_-,r_A]$, $\operatorname{polyA}(r)<0$.  polyD has leading coefficient
  $2P(P+Q-1)>0$ and is negative at both $r_-$ and the forced upper endpoint
  $r_+$; so $\operatorname{polyD}(r)<0$.  Finally
  $\operatorname{polyC}=\mathcal BP\operatorname{polyD}+Q\operatorname{polyA}$
  with $\mathcal B,P,Q>0$ is negative.  No numerical certificate is used.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.NativeOppositePure.fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_acute_orthogonal
lean.code:
theorem fderiv_nativeLengthController_surjective_of_acute_orthogonal
    {p t q h l u v : ℝ}
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hq : 1 < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q)
    (hu : u ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hv : v ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (hphys : NativeLengthPhysical p t q h l (orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v))
    (hzero : nativeLengthController p t q h l (orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v) = 0)
    (hT : Real.arcsin (q * orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v 1) +
      Real.arcsin (q * orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v 2) < Real.pi / 2) :
    Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeLengthController p t q h l)
      (orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v)) := by
  let L := orderedCoreHalfLengths u q v
  let α := Real.arcsin (L 0)
  let β := Real.arcsin (L 3)
  let γ := Real.arcsin (q * L 1)
  let δ := Real.arcsin (q * L 2)
  have hq0 : 0 < q := by linarith
  obtain ⟨hα, hβ, hγ, hδ⟩ := coreHalfLengths_angles_acute hu.1 hu.2 hq hv.1 hv.2
  obtain ⟨a0, a3, a1, a2⟩ := coreHalfLengths_angle_data hu.1 hu.2 hq hv.1 hv.2
  have hs0 : Real.sin α = L 0 := Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith [a0.1.1]) a0.1.2.le
  have hs3 : Real.sin β = L 3 := Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith [a3.1.1]) a3.1.2.le
  have hs1 : Real.sin γ = q * L 1 := Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith [a1.1.1]) a1.1.2.le
  have hs2 : Real.sin δ = q * L 2 := Real.sin_arcsin (by linarith [a2.1.1]) a2.1.2.le
  have ha : StrictAngles q h α β γ δ := by
    refine ⟨hα, hβ, hγ, hδ, ?_⟩
    rw [hs2]
    have hh2 := hphys.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
    convert hh2 using 1
    field_simp
    rfl
  have hL : ![Real.sin α, Real.sin γ / q, Real.sin δ / q, Real.sin β] = L := by
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> simp [hs0, hs3, hs1, hs2, ne_of_gt hq0]
  have hx : StrictAngles q h (![α + β, α, γ] 1)
      (![α + β, α, γ] 0 - ![α + β, α, γ] 1)
      (![α + β, α, γ] 2) ((γ + δ) - ![α + β, α, γ] 2) := by simpa using ha
  have hnative := nativeLengthController_splitHalfLengths
    (p := p) (t := t) (h := h) (l := l) (x := ![α + β, α, γ]) (T := γ + δ)
    (ne_of_gt hq0) hx.1 hx.2.1 hx.2.2.1 hx.2.2.2.1
  have hz : (nativeHalfClosure p t q h l α β γ δ,
      turnDefect p t q h l α β γ δ) = 0 := by
    have he : nativeLengthController p t q h l
        ![Real.sin α, Real.sin γ / q, Real.sin δ / q, Real.sin β] =
        (nativeHalfClosure p t q h l α β γ δ, turnDefect p t q h l α β γ δ) := by
      simpa [splitHalfLengths, nativeSplitController] using hnative
    rw [← he, hL]
    exact hzero
  obtain ⟨htan1, htan2⟩ := coreHalfLengths_tan_products hu.1 hu.2 hq hv.1 hv.2
  have htaneq : Real.tan α * Real.tan δ = Real.tan β * Real.tan γ := htan1.trans htan2.symm
  have htan_gt : 1 < Real.tan α * Real.tan δ :=
    coreHalfLengths_tan_product_gt_one hu.1 hu.2 hq hv.1 hv.2
  have hcos := coreHalfLengths_normalized_cos hu.1 hu.2 hq hv.1 hv.2
  by_contra hn
  have hn' : ¬Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ (nativeLengthController p t q h l)
      ![Real.sin α, Real.sin γ / q, Real.sin δ / q, Real.sin β]) := by rwa [hL]
  obtain ⟨z⟩ := incidentProjectiveRankLoss_of_angles hp hp1 hl hl1 ht htq hq hh hhq
    ha hT htaneq htan_gt hcos hz hn'
  exact z.false

Take the core angles of \cref{lem:nrn_core_trig}: they are acute, and
  the high wall $hL_2<1$ gives $(h/q)\sin\delta<1$, so they are strict.

  hypothesis is $\gamma+\delta<\pi/2$.  If $DN(L)$ were not surjective,

  \cref{thm:nrn_packet_false} rules out.

blocks.body:
Let $\kappa\colon\ZMod n\to\RR$ with $\kappa_i\ne\kappa_{i+1}$ for all
  $i$, $\kappa_0=1=\kappa_H$ and $H\ne0$.  Then the natural representative
  of $H$ satisfies $2\le H\le n-2$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.repeated_maximum_index_separation
lean.code:
theorem repeated_maximum_index_separation {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H : ZMod n}
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hzero : κ 0 = 1) (hH : κ H = 1) (hH0 : H ≠ 0) :
    2 ≤ H.val ∧ H.val + 2 ≤ n := by
  have hv : 0 < H.val := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (fun hz => hH0 ((ZMod.val_eq_zero H).mp hz))
  have hvn := H.val_lt
  have hnot1 : H.val ≠ 1 := by
    intro hv1
    have he : H = 1 := by simpa [hv1] using (ZMod.natCast_zmod_val H).symm
    have hn := hne 0
    simp only [zero_add, hzero, ← he, hH, ne_eq, not_true_eq_false] at hn
  have hnotlast : H.val + 1 ≠ n := by
    intro he
    have hwrap : H + 1 = 0 := by
      rw [← ZMod.natCast_zmod_val H]
      norm_cast
      rw [he, ZMod.natCast_self]
    have hn := hne H
    rw [hwrap, hH, hzero] at hn
    exact hn rfl
  constructor <;> omega

blocks.tex:
$0<H<n$ since $H\ne0$.  If $H=1$ then $\kappa_0=\kappa_1$, contradicting
  adjacent-unequality at $0$.  If $H+1=n$ then $H+1=0$ in $\ZMod n$ (the
  cyclic last edge) and $\kappa_H=\kappa_{H+1}$, contradicting
  adjacent-unequality at $H$.  Hence $2\le H$ and $H+2\le n$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_repeated_normalized_maximum
lean.code:
theorem nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_repeated_normalized_maximum
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H : ZMod n}
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hle : ∀ i, κ i ≤ 1)
    (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hzero : κ 0 = 1) (hH : κ H = 1) (hH0 : H ≠ 0) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := repeated_maximum_index_separation hne hzero hH hH0
  let F := firstPairFrame hlo hhi
  have hp1 : κ 1 < 1 := lt_of_le_of_ne (hle 1) (by
    intro he
    exact hne 0 (by simpa [hzero] using he.symm))
  have ht1 : κ (H - 1) < 1 := lt_of_le_of_ne (hle (H - 1)) (by
    intro he
    exact hne (H - 1) (by simpa [hH] using he))
  have hh1 : κ (H + 1) < 1 := lt_of_le_of_ne (hle (H + 1)) (by
    intro he
    exact hne H (by rw [hH, he]))
  have hl1 : κ (-1) < 1 := lt_of_le_of_ne (hle (-1)) (by
    intro he
    exact hne (-1) (by simpa [hzero] using he))
  have hpred : ((H.val - 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) = H - 1 := by
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega : 1 ≤ H.val), ZMod.natCast_zmod_val, Nat.cast_one]
  have hlast : ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) = -1 := by
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega : 1 ≤ n), ZMod.natCast_self]
    simp
  have hnext : ((H.val + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) = H + 1 := by simp
  have hstart : F.start κ = ![1, κ (H - 1), 1, κ (-1)] := by
    simpa [F, hpred, hlast, hH] using firstPairFrame_start hlo hhi κ hzero
  have hfinish : F.finish κ = ![κ 1, 1, κ (H + 1), 1] := by
    simpa [F, hnext, hH] using firstPairFrame_finish hlo hhi κ hzero
  exact F.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_repeated_maximum hstart hfinish
    (hκ 1) hp1 (hκ (H - 1)) ht1 (hκ (H + 1)) hh1 (hκ (-1)) hl1

blocks.tex:
(1) \Cref{thm:nrn_repeated_zero} gives a physical native zero $L$ for
  $(p,t,1,h,l)$, and \cref{thm:nrn_equal_pure_rank} makes $DN(L)$
  surjective.  \Cref{lem:nfp_to_anchor} (with $q=1$) packages $(F,L)$ as a
  regular anchor (\verb|RegularFourAnchor.ofNative|).

  (2) \Cref{lem:nrn_repeated_separation} gives $2\le H$, $H+2\le n$, so
  \cref{lem:nfp_frame} with $i=H$ gives the frame $0<H-1<H<n-1$ with start
  $(1,\kappa_{H-1},\kappa_H,\kappa_{n-1})=(1,t,1,l)$ and finish
  $(\kappa_1,\kappa_H,\kappa_{H+1},1)=(p,1,h,1)$, where $p=\kappa_1$,
  $t=\kappa_{H-1}$, $h=\kappa_{H+1}$, $l=\kappa_{-1}$ (the casts of the
  natural numbers $H-1$, $H+1$, $n-1$ are $H-1$, $H+1$, $-1$ in $\ZMod n$).
  These four readings are positive, at most $1$ because $1$ is the global
  maximum, and different from $1$ because each is adjacent to $0$ or to
  $H$, where the reading is $1$.  Apply (1).  These are the four literal
  edges incident to the two maxima; every intervening reading stays in the
  word, and there is no bound on their number or values.

blocks.label: thm:nrn_negative_anchor
blocks.title: anchors at two negative terminal flags
blocks.body:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If a frame $F$ of $\kappa$ has start $(1,t,q,l)$ and finish
      $(p,q,h,1)$ with the hypotheses of \cref{thm:nrn_negative_regular},
      then $\kappa$ has a regular four-edge anchor.
    \item Let $\kappa>0$ be adjacent-unequal, $\kappa_0=1<\kappa_H$,
      $\kappa_i<\kappa_H$ for all $i\ne H$, and let $0$ be a highest
      secondary peak for $H$ (\cref{def:four_active_secondary_peak}).  If
      the forward and backward terminal flags are negative,
      \[
        \Phi(\kappa_1,\kappa_{H-1},\kappa_H,\kappa_{-1})<0,\qquad
        \Phi(\kappa_{-1},\kappa_{H+1},\kappa_H,\kappa_1)<0,
      \]
      then $\kappa$ has a regular four-edge anchor on the edges
      $0,H-1,H,n-1$.
  \end{enumerate}

lean.code:
theorem HighestSecondaryPeak.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_negative_terminals
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {κ : ZMod n → ℝ} {H : ZMod n}
    (hq : HighestSecondaryPeak κ H 0)
    (hκ : ∀ i, 0 < κ i) (hne : ∀ i, κ i ≠ κ (i + 1))
    (hzero : κ 0 = 1) (hH : 1 < κ H)
    (hglobal : ∀ i, i ≠ H → κ i < κ H)
    (hforward : firstPairFlag (κ 1) (κ (H - 1)) (κ H) (κ (-1)) < 0)
    (hbackward : firstPairFlag (κ (-1)) (κ (H + 1)) (κ H) (κ 1) < 0) :
    Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, ha, hak, hkb, hbn, _, _, _⟩ :=
    hq.exists_mountain hne (by simpa only [hzero] using hH)
  simp only [sub_zero] at hak hkb
  have hlo : 2 ≤ H.val := by omega
  have hhi : H.val + 2 ≤ n := by omega
  let : Fact (1 < n) := ⟨by omega⟩
  let F := firstPairFrame hlo hhi
  have hp : κ 1 < 1 := by simpa [hzero] using hq.is_peak.2
  have hl : κ (-1) < 1 := by simpa [hzero] using hq.is_peak.1
  have ht : κ (H - 1) < κ H := hglobal _ (by simp)
  have hh : κ (H + 1) < κ H := hglobal _ (by simp)
  have hpred := natPred_val_residue hq.ne_global.symm
  have hlast : ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ZMod n) = -1 := by
    rw [Nat.cast_sub (by omega : 1 ≤ n), ZMod.natCast_self]
    simp
  have hstart : F.start κ = ![1, κ (H - 1), κ H, κ (-1)] := by
    simpa [F, hpred, hlast] using firstPairFrame_start hlo hhi κ hzero
  have hfinish : F.finish κ = ![κ 1, κ H, κ (H + 1), 1] := by
    simpa [F] using firstPairFrame_finish hlo hhi κ hzero
  exact F.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_negative_corners hstart hfinish
    (hκ 1) hp (hκ (-1)) hl (hκ (H - 1)) ht (hκ (H + 1)) hh hH hforward hbackward

theorem FourActiveSlots.Frame.nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_negative_corners

    (hfinish : F.finish κ = ![p, q, h, 1])
    (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hl : 0 < l) (hl1 : l < 1)
    (ht : 0 < t) (htq : t < q) (hh : 0 < h) (hhq : h < q) (hq : 1 < q)

    (hreflected : firstPairFlag l h q p < 0) : Nonempty (RegularFourAnchor κ) := by
  obtain ⟨L, hphysical, hzero, hregular⟩ :=
    exists_nativeLength_regular_of_negative_corners
      hp hp1 hl hl1 ht htq hh hhq hq hflag hreflected
  exact ⟨RegularFourAnchor.ofNative F hstart hfinish hphysical hzero hregular⟩

(1) \Cref{thm:nrn_negative_regular} and \cref{lem:nfp_to_anchor}.

  (2) The mountain of \cref{lem:four_active_mountain} (with secondary peak
  $0$) gives offsets $2\le a\le H\le b\le n-2$, so $2\le H$ and
  $H+2\le n$; this lemma is proved in
  \cref{chap:discrete_mountain_anchor_transport} (\cref{thm:mt_mountain}).
  \Cref{lem:nfp_frame} with $i=H$ gives the frame $0,H-1,H,n-1$ with start
  $(1,\kappa_{H-1},\kappa_H,\kappa_{-1})$ and finish
  $(\kappa_1,\kappa_H,\kappa_{H+1},1)$ (the cast of $H-1$ uses $H\ne0$,
  \verb|natPred_val_residue|).  Put $p=\kappa_1$, $t=\kappa_{H-1}$,
  $q=\kappa_H$, $h=\kappa_{H+1}$, $l=\kappa_{-1}$.  Positivity gives
  $p,t,h,l>0$.  Since $0$ is a strict local maximum with $\kappa_0=1$,
  $p<1$ and $l<1$.  Strict unique global maximality at $H$ gives $t<q$,
  $h<q$, and $q>1$ is a hypothesis.  The forward terminal flag is literally
  $\Phi(p,t,q,l)$ and the backward one is literally $\Phi(l,h,q,p)$ --- the
  two negative-corner flags.  Apply (1).  No bound on the intervening
  readings or on $n$ is used.
